﴿Say: Have you considered, if this is from Allah and you have disbelieved in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to something similar and believed while you remained arrogant? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (46:10) Say to them: "Have you ever considered: if this speech is from Allah and you have rejected it [what will your end be]? A witness from the Children of Israel has already borne testimony to a similar scripture. He believed, and you remained in your pride. Allah does not guide such wrongdoers."

It is possible that this refers to an event in which a person or a group from the Children of Israel, seeing that Quranic teachings resemble the Torah and other books, believed, because those who believed in the heavenly scriptures knew that this book says what is in those books. Some narrations state that this verse was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Salam, but what stands in the way of this is that he became a Muslim in Medina, and this surah is Meccan. There are also narrations that this verse is Medinan, because it was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Salam, while there are also narrations that it is Meccan and has no connection with the event of Abdullah ibn Salam.

It is also possible that it points to an event in Mecca, in which someone from the People of the Book believed, although the People of the Book were very few there. In Meccan circumstances, their belief would have had great importance, because the polytheists were unlettered, and in such a society the belief of People of the Book carried weight. This is why the Qur'an pointed to the testimony of the People of the Book in several places, and presented it to refute the polytheists who denied the Qur'an without proof, without evidence, without knowledge and skill, and without any book or heavenly tradition.

But the point to understand here is that the Qur'an has employed a hypothetical mode of argument here: "Have you considered that if this is from Allah and…" The purpose of this style of argument is to create wavering in the insistence of the polytheists, to reduce the intensity of their insistence, to cool their hostility, and to create in them some fear and caution, so that they do not advance so far in denial. And the argument is made that although you do not accept it, if it turns out to be true, then your end will be very bad. Therefore, keeping this supposition and possibility in view, be cautious: if this turns out to be true, all those punishments with which Muhammad ﷺ warns you will come upon you. So pause before denying the Messenger ﷺ, and reflect on this call, before you fall into such a dangerous end or before the possibility of such an end arises, especially in circumstances where a person or group from the Children of Israel has already given testimony that the nature of this book is like the speech of Allah, and on that basis believed. And when this book came first to you, in your language, through a man of your own, you are proud and deny it. This is clear injustice. It is abandoning clear truth and going forward, and in that case all your deeds will be lost and the punishment of Allah will come.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (46:10) In short, the Qur'an adopts every method to make people understand. It employs various styles of speech so that it may remove the doubts in human hearts, and it strives to convey its call to people's hearts through different paths. The various styles the Qur'an has adopted contain lessons and guidance for the callers who come later. Although for both Allah and His Messenger ﷺ the Qur'an was certainly the truth, the word of Allah, and there was no matter of doubt or possibility in it, yet this style was also adopted to make people understand, so that perhaps in this way the intensity of opposition might decrease.

The discussion then continues regarding what they used to say about the Qur'an, Islam, and the Islamic system, and an examination of it. They also used to put forward another justification for their denial and disbelief. This is the talk of the arrogant and those who consider themselves to be of high rank.

﴿And those who disbelieved say to those who believed: If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it. And since they have not been guided by it, they will surely say: This is an ancient falsehood.﴾ (46:11) "Those who have refused to accept say about the believers: If accepting this book were a good thing, these people would not have outstripped us in it. Since they were not guided by it, they will surely say: This is an ancient lie."

In the early days of Islam, the poor and the slaves rushed toward Islam. Therefore the great and the arrogant did not regard it favourably. This stuck in their eyes, and they used to say: If this religion were a good religion, would these people have known more and been more shrewd than us? They could not have preceded us in it, because we have more knowledge than them, we are more aware, and we have greater discernment between good and bad.

But the matter was not like this. The reason these great ones did not accept Islam was not that they doubted it, or that they were ignorant and did not know that the Noble Qur'an is pure truth, or that it contains no news. Rather, out of arrogance they acted this way, and they regarded accepting the truth as a task beneath them. Then they thought that in the present social order they would not retain the status they enjoyed in society, and the interests they possessed would not remain. Another reason was that regarding the ways of their forefathers they thought that this was a matter worthy of pride, whereas for those who rushed toward Islam at its first call, these obstacles did not exist that had stopped the great ones.

It is always the case that great people do not accept the truth. Because of pride and arrogance it is not possible for them to bow before the truth. Therefore they do not respond to the voice of nature, and they do not accept the proof. This pride and arrogance dictates to them that they should be stubborn and not accept it. They fabricate false excuses and make the falsest of false claims. Such great people never admit their mistakes. They are concerned with making their own selves the axis of life, and they want to continue as they are the axis in their present society.

﴿And since they have not been guided by it, they will surely say: This is an ancient falsehood.﴾ (46:11) Yes, if these people did not accept guidance, then necessarily there must be some defect in the truth. For great people cannot make mistakes! But these people presented themselves, in their own eyes and in the eyes of the common masses, as a kind of innocent creature free from error.

In any case, the passage on revelation and this study journey end with a reference to the Book of Moses, that the Qur'an is a link in the chain of earlier heavenly scriptures. Especially the Torah and the Qur'an have a deep resemblance, because the mission of Jesus (peace be upon him) was a completion of the Torah itself. Earlier, a reference was also made to a witness from the Children of Israel.

﴿And before it was the Book of Moses as a guide and mercy. And this is a Book confirming it in the Arabic tongue, to warn those who wronged and as good tidings to the doers of good.﴾ (46:12) "Before this, the Book of Moses came as a guide and mercy, and this Book, which confirms it, has come in the Arabic language, to warn the wrongdoers and to give good news to those who adopt a righteous course."

The Qur'an has repeatedly pointed to its relationship with the earlier heavenly scriptures, especially the Torah, because the book of Jesus was its completion and his mission was a continuation of the Torah. The original law was in the Torah itself. This is why it was given the title of imam and mercy, whereas every messengership is a mercy for this earth and its inhabitants, in this world and in the Hereafter.

﴿And this is a Book confirming it in the Arabic tongue.﴾ (46:12) This confirms the original books and original teachings on which all heavenly religions rest. This book confirms the system according to which all people of religion have walked. And this book confirms the straight path that leads human beings to Allah.

The phrase "in the Arabic tongue" was said here so that the favour bestowed upon the Arabs would be made manifest: that this book was sent down in their language. They were reminded that Allah had shown them special grace and particular kindness, in making them the bearers of this call and in granting their language the honour that the mighty Qur'an was revealed in it. The purpose was not language alone, but this.

﴿To warn those who wronged and as good tidings to the doers of good.﴾ (46:12) "So that it may warn the wrongdoers and give good tidings to those who do good."

At the end of this first lesson, a picture is drawn of the reward of the doers of good, and it is shown that the Noble Qur'an brings you this good news, provided they proclaim absolute monotheism and the lordship of Allah, then remain firm upon it and fulfil its requirements.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah 46, verses 4–12 (part 1 of 2)**

Verses 4 to 12

Allah instructs the Prophet (ﷺ) to present to his people this cosmic testimony. The universe is an open book. Argument and debate cannot be conducted against this book, because it lies before everyone. It addresses human nature, and its logic and manner of speech are also natural. There is a deep connection between this book of the universe and the human nature. It cannot be suppressed, and no one can deceive anyone through it. This is a natural question:

﴿Show me what it is that they have created from the earth﴾ (46:4). "Show me, then, what they have created in the earth." It was not possible, and it is still not possible, that any of these man-made gods, whether stones, trees, jinn or angels, has created any part or thing of the earth. Natural reasoning, the reality of the matter, and every thing itself cry out that there is nothing. They have not created anything at all.

﴿Or do they have a share in the heavens?﴾ (46:4) "Or do they have any share in the heavens?" No person can even claim that the aforementioned gods have any share or partnership in the heavens. Even a superficial glance at the heavens shows how great the Creator of the universe is, and that He is One. In a single look, a reasonable person casts aside all misguidance and all the false gods. Allah, who is the Creator of man, knows that a deep contemplation of this universe alone transforms a human being. Therefore Allah repeatedly draws man's attention: cast a glance upon this open book of the universe, reflect upon its order, and ask the signals that come to your heart and mind from this universe what testimony they give.

After this, a question is posed in order to close the path of some extremely misguided people and to establish the proof against them. Sometimes, advancing further in misguidance, someone may boast that he has a counterfeit proof for his shirk, or may make some other excuse, although in reality he has no proof or argument. Therefore the Qur'an, before such people can speak, makes its demand: bring forth your proof, if you have any. The Qur'an also teaches them the method of reasoning, that is, what the correct procedure is for arriving at a decision.

﴿Bring me a Book before this, or any remnant of knowledge, if you are truthful﴾ (46:4). "Bring me a book that came before this one, or any remnant of knowledge that you have, if you are truthful." Either present a true book of Allah, or bring any trace that remains of the heavenly scriptures. All the heavenly books revealed before the Qur'an bear witness in support of the Qur'an that Allah alone is the Creator, that He alone is the Manager of the universe, and that He creates all things in a measured and proper manner. None of these books accepts the fables of multiple gods. Nor does any heavenly book contain any knowledge, influence or text stating that any of these gods created any part of the heavens or the earth, or had any share in creating anything.

The Qur'an also presents before them the testimony of the universe itself. The testimony of the universe is decisive testimony. In this way the Qur'an deprives their beliefs of any argument or proof, and also teaches them what the correct manner of debate and reasoning is. All these matters are taught in a single verse, whose words are few but forceful and decisive.

After this, the Qur'an presents to them the point that those things which you make into gods and then call upon are in reality without any substance. They do not even hear your call. Even if you call upon them throughout your lives in this world, and on the Day of Judgment, they will clearly deny you. Therefore, reflect upon this conduct of yours.

﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon, besides Allah, those who will not answer him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are heedless of their calling? And when mankind is gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ (46:5–6). "Who is more astray than the one who calls upon, besides Allah, those who cannot respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are even unaware of the calls of those who call upon them? And when mankind is gathered, these gods will become enemies to their worshippers and will deny their worship."

Some people regarded idols as deities in themselves. Some regarded them as deities, considering them to be likenesses of angels or righteous people. Some regarded trees as deities, and some regarded angels and Satan as deities. None of these could respond to the one who called upon them, or, if they heard the call, they could not benefit him. Stones and trees could neither hear nor respond. The angels also gave no answer to this conduct of the polytheists. As for the devils, they continued to whisper suggestions in order to lead them further astray. When the Day of Judgment comes and people are raised, all these gods that were worshipped will deny the worship of their misguided devotees. So much so that Satan, whose very work is to misguide people, will say:

﴿And when the matter has been decided, Satan will say: "Indeed, Allah promised you a true promise, and I promised you, but I failed you. I had no authority over you, except that I called you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I deny your association of me with Allah before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment"﴾ (14:22).

In this way the Qur'an presents them before their own claims and their own ideas, showing what the outcome of these claims will be in this world and in the Hereafter. Earlier they were shown the signs of the universe, which deny the beliefs of shirk. In both cases, what is established is that the only God of this universe is the Lord of the worlds, and that the very good of the polytheists themselves, in this world and in the Hereafter, lies in their reconsidering these ideas.

Here the Qur'an criticises those idolaters who were calling upon idols that could neither benefit nor harm them. At the time of the revelation of the Qur'an, such traditional living and dead deities existed. But this verse is not limited to those idols, which were called upon in a particular time and place, in a particular form, and upon which hopes were placed. The verse is very broad, and it includes all the deities besides Allah that will exist in any time or place: those whom the common people call upon, on whom they place their hopes, and who can bring them no benefit or harm, because the one who brings benefit and harm is Allah alone. In short, shirk is not limited to the simple form that existed among the Arabs at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an. There are many people who associate with Allah those in positions of authority. They associate officials, and they associate great capitalists. They place their hopes in them, call upon them, and yet all of them are extremely helpless and weak, and they cannot give any benefit. They do not even possess power over their own benefit and harm. To call upon such people is shirk, to place hopes in them is shirk, and to fear them is shirk. However, this shirk is a hidden shirk, and most people fall into it unconsciously.

* * *

After this, a discussion takes place concerning the position of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his true call. Their ideas about shirk have been thoroughly examined. Now it is explained how wrong and unreasonable their position is regarding revelation and the Islamic call.

﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say of the truth when it comes to them, "This is obvious magic." Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say: "If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me against Allah at all. He is most knowing of what you say about it. Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful." Say: "I am not something new among the messengers, and I do not know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am only a clear warner." Say: "Have you considered, if it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to something like it and believed while you are arrogant? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people." Those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it." And since they have not been guided by it, they will surely say, "This is an ancient falsehood." And before it was the Book of Moses, a guide and a mercy. And this is a confirming Book in Arabic, to warn those who wronged and as good tidings to the doers of good﴾ (46:7–12).

The Qur'an's verses and its call are such that there is no doubt about them. They are very clear, appealing and manifest statements. Yet these people are so base, obstinate and wretched that they make this comment about the truth:

﴿This is obvious magic﴾ (46:7). "This is evident magic." But the Islamic call and magic differ in their nature and their subject matter. The aims of a prophet and of a sorcerer are entirely different. In this way, their wrong position is attacked, a position for which they have neither proof nor a valid answer, because the call of the Prophet (ﷺ) is very clear and consists of manifest signs.

Next, their other objection is taken up, which they used to raise: that this Qur'an is fabricated by Muhammad (ﷺ) himself, that it is attributed to Allah, and that it is a fabrication. The Qur'an presents this doubt in the form of a question: is this even a question at all? Could any reasonable person think such a thing?

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ (46:8). "Or do they say that he has invented it?" That is, have they become so audacious that they make such a statement, when even the thought of it cannot be conceived?

The Prophet (ﷺ) is told to answer this question in the manner befitting a prophet, because this question is very senseless. Through this answer, it should become apparent that he is well aware of his duties, that he is well aware of his Lord, and that he fully appreciates the true values and true powers of this universe.

﴿Say: "If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me against Allah at all. He is most knowing of what you say about it. Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful"﴾ (46:8). "Say: If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me against Allah at all. He knows best what you say about it. He is sufficient as a witness between me and you, and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful." Say to them: why would I invent a lie? For whose benefit would I invent it? For what aims would I do so? Is it so that you may believe in me and obey me? But what help can you give me?

﴿If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me against Allah at all﴾ (46:8). "If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me in any way against Allah." Because of my fabrication, He will certainly call me to account. Therefore, if you are with me and believe in me, what benefit would that be to me? When Allah calls me to account for the fabrication, what could you do at that time? You are very helpless and weak. What help could you give me?

This is an answer that befits a prophet, one who takes guidance from Allah and in whose sight nothing in this universe is visible except Allah. He sees only the power of Allah. It is also a logical and reasonable refutation, if anyone uses his intellect. By answering them, the Prophet (ﷺ) adds this:

﴿He is most knowing of what you say about it﴾ (46:8). "He knows best what you say about it." That is, what you do and say. And for those things that Allah knows, He will certainly punish you.

﴿Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you﴾ (46:8). "He is sufficient as a witness between me and you." Allah will both bear witness and make the decision, and the witness and judgment of Allah are sufficient.

﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ (46:8). "And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful." He is merciful to you, and through His mercy He guides you, and He forgives the errors you have committed, since previous deeds are pardoned after faith.

This refutation contains both a threat and a warning for them, and also an encouragement and an inducement to faith. In every way, Allah's effort is to change human hearts. The very fibre of the human being is touched, in the hope that the melody of faith may emerge. The listeners are given the impression that this matter is very important, and that the foolish things these people say are merely childish talk, mere claims they keep making. The message in the heart of the Great Caller, the thing to which he invites, is very great, while these people have no awareness of its importance and greatness.

﴿To warn those who wronged and as good tidings to the doers of good.﴾ (46:12) "So that it may warn the wrongdoers and give good tidings to those who do good."

At the end of this first lesson, a picture is drawn of the reward of the doers of good, and it is shown that the Noble Qur'an brings you this good news, provided they proclaim absolute monotheism and the lordship of Allah, then remain firm upon it and fulfil its requirements.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah 46, verses 4–12 (part 1 of 2)**

Verses 4 to 12

Allah instructs the Prophet (ﷺ) to present to his people this cosmic testimony. The universe is an open book. Argument and debate cannot be conducted against this book, because it lies before everyone. It addresses human nature, and its logic and manner of speech are also natural. There is a deep connection between this book of the universe and the human nature. It cannot be suppressed, and no one can deceive anyone through it. This is a natural question:

﴿Show me what it is that they have created from the earth﴾ (46:4). "Show me, then, what they have created in the earth." It was not possible, and it is still not possible, that any of these man-made gods, whether stones, trees, jinn or angels, has created any part or thing of the earth. Natural reasoning, the reality of the matter, and every thing itself cry out that there is nothing. They have not created anything at all.

﴿Or do they have a share in the heavens?﴾ (46:4) "Or do they have any share in the heavens?" No person can even claim that the aforementioned gods have any share or partnership in the heavens. Even a superficial glance at the heavens shows how great the Creator of the universe is, and that He is One. In a single look, a reasonable person casts aside all misguidance and all the false gods. Allah, who is the Creator of man, knows that a deep contemplation of this universe alone transforms a human being. Therefore Allah repeatedly draws man's attention: cast a glance upon this open book of the universe, reflect upon its order, and ask the signals that come to your heart and mind from this universe what testimony they give.

After this, a question is posed in order to close the path of some extremely misguided people and to establish the proof against them. Sometimes, advancing further in misguidance, someone may boast that he has a counterfeit proof for his shirk, or may make some other excuse, although in reality he has no proof or argument. Therefore the Qur'an, before such people can speak, makes its demand: bring forth your proof, if you have any. The Qur'an also teaches them the method of reasoning, that is, what the correct procedure is for arriving at a decision.

﴿Bring me a Book before this, or any remnant of knowledge, if you are truthful﴾ (46:4). "Bring me a book that came before this one, or any remnant of knowledge that you have, if you are truthful." Either present a true book of Allah, or bring any trace that remains of the heavenly scriptures. All the heavenly books revealed before the Qur'an bear witness in support of the Qur'an that Allah alone is the Creator, that He alone is the Manager of the universe, and that He creates all things in a measured and proper manner. None of these books accepts the fables of multiple gods. Nor does any heavenly book contain any knowledge, influence or text stating that any of these gods created any part of the heavens or the earth, or had any share in creating anything.

The Qur'an also presents before them the testimony of the universe itself. The testimony of the universe is decisive testimony. In this way the Qur'an deprives their beliefs of any argument or proof, and also teaches them what the correct manner of debate and reasoning is. All these matters are taught in a single verse, whose words are few but forceful and decisive.

After this, the Qur'an presents to them the point that those things which you make into gods and then call upon are in reality without any substance. They do not even hear your call. Even if you call upon them throughout your lives in this world, and on the Day of Judgment, they will clearly deny you. Therefore, reflect upon this conduct of yours.

﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon, besides Allah, those who will not answer him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are heedless of their calling? And when mankind is gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ (46:5–6). "Who is more astray than the one who calls upon, besides Allah, those who cannot respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are even unaware of the calls of those who call upon them? And when mankind is gathered, these gods will become enemies to their worshippers and will deny their worship."

Some people regarded idols as deities in themselves. Some regarded them as deities, considering them to be likenesses of angels or righteous people. Some regarded trees as deities, and some regarded angels and Satan as deities. None of these could respond to the one who called upon them, or, if they heard the call, they could not benefit him. Stones and trees could neither hear nor respond. The angels also gave no answer to this conduct of the polytheists. As for the devils, they continued to whisper suggestions in order to lead them further astray. When the Day of Judgment comes and people are raised, all these gods that were worshipped will deny the worship of their misguided devotees. So much so that Satan, whose very work is to misguide people, will say:

﴿And when the matter has been decided, Satan will say: "Indeed, Allah promised you a true promise, and I promised you, but I failed you. I had no authority over you, except that I called you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I deny your association of me with Allah before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment"﴾ (14:22).

In this way the Qur'an presents them before their own claims and their own ideas, showing what the outcome of these claims will be in this world and in the Hereafter. Earlier they were shown the signs of the universe, which deny the beliefs of shirk. In both cases, what is established is that the only God of this universe is the Lord of the worlds, and that the very good of the polytheists themselves, in this world and in the Hereafter, lies in their reconsidering these ideas.

Here the Qur'an criticises those idolaters who were calling upon idols that could neither benefit nor harm them. At the time of the revelation of the Qur'an, such traditional living and dead deities existed. But this verse is not limited to those idols, which were called upon in a particular time and place, in a particular form, and upon which hopes were placed. The verse is very broad, and it includes all the deities besides Allah that will exist in any time or place: those whom the common people call upon, on whom they place their hopes, and who can bring them no benefit or harm, because the one who brings benefit and harm is Allah alone. In short, shirk is not limited to the simple form that existed among the Arabs at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an. There are many people who associate with Allah those in positions of authority. They associate officials, and they associate great capitalists. They place their hopes in them, call upon them, and yet all of them are extremely helpless and weak, and they cannot give any benefit. They do not even possess power over their own benefit and harm. To call upon such people is shirk, to place hopes in them is shirk, and to fear them is shirk. However, this shirk is a hidden shirk, and most people fall into it unconsciously.

* * *

After this, a discussion takes place concerning the position of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his true call. Their ideas about shirk have been thoroughly examined. Now it is explained how wrong and unreasonable their position is regarding revelation and the Islamic call.

﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say of the truth when it comes to them, "This is obvious magic." Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say: "If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me against Allah at all. He is most knowing of what you say about it. Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful." Say: "I am not something new among the messengers, and I do not know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am only a clear warner." Say: "Have you considered, if it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to something like it and believed while you are arrogant? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people." Those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it." And since they have not been guided by it, they will surely say, "This is an ancient falsehood." And before it was the Book of Moses, a guide and a mercy. And this is a confirming Book in Arabic, to warn those who wronged and as good tidings to the doers of good﴾ (46:7–12).

The Qur'an's verses and its call are such that there is no doubt about them. They are very clear, appealing and manifest statements. Yet these people are so base, obstinate and wretched that they make this comment about the truth:

﴿This is obvious magic﴾ (46:7). "This is evident magic." But the Islamic call and magic differ in their nature and their subject matter. The aims of a prophet and of a sorcerer are entirely different. In this way, their wrong position is attacked, a position for which they have neither proof nor a valid answer, because the call of the Prophet (ﷺ) is very clear and consists of manifest signs.

Next, their other objection is taken up, which they used to raise: that this Qur'an is fabricated by Muhammad (ﷺ) himself, that it is attributed to Allah, and that it is a fabrication. The Qur'an presents this doubt in the form of a question: is this even a question at all? Could any reasonable person think such a thing?

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ (46:8). "Or do they say that he has invented it?" That is, have they become so audacious that they make such a statement, when even the thought of it cannot be conceived?

The Prophet (ﷺ) is told to answer this question in the manner befitting a prophet, because this question is very senseless. Through this answer, it should become apparent that he is well aware of his duties, that he is well aware of his Lord, and that he fully appreciates the true values and true powers of this universe.

﴿Say: "If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me against Allah at all. He is most knowing of what you say about it. Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful"﴾ (46:8). "Say: If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me against Allah at all. He knows best what you say about it. He is sufficient as a witness between me and you, and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful." Say to them: why would I invent a lie? For whose benefit would I invent it? For what aims would I do so? Is it so that you may believe in me and obey me? But what help can you give me?

﴿If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me against Allah at all﴾ (46:8). "If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me in any way against Allah." Because of my fabrication, He will certainly call me to account. Therefore, if you are with me and believe in me, what benefit would that be to me? When Allah calls me to account for the fabrication, what could you do at that time? You are very helpless and weak. What help could you give me?

This is an answer that befits a prophet, one who takes guidance from Allah and in whose sight nothing in this universe is visible except Allah. He sees only the power of Allah. It is also a logical and reasonable refutation, if anyone uses his intellect. By answering them, the Prophet (ﷺ) adds this:

﴿He is most knowing of what you say about it﴾ (46:8). "He knows best what you say about it." That is, what you do and say. And for those things that Allah knows, He will certainly punish you.

﴿Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you﴾ (46:8). "He is sufficient as a witness between me and you." Allah will both bear witness and make the decision, and the witness and judgment of Allah are sufficient.

﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ (46:8). "And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful." He is merciful to you, and through His mercy He guides you, and He forgives the errors you have committed, since previous deeds are pardoned after faith.

This refutation contains both a threat and a warning for them, and also an encouragement and an inducement to faith. In every way, Allah's effort is to change human hearts. The very fibre of the human being is touched, in the hope that the melody of faith may emerge. The listeners are given the impression that this matter is very important, and that the foolish things these people say are merely childish talk, mere claims they keep making. The message in the heart of the Great Caller, the thing to which he invites, is very great, while these people have no awareness of its importance and greatness.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 46, verses 4–12 (part 2 of 2):

Another angle is also used to answer their objection to revelation. Revelation is an event for which there are examples in history, and millions of people believe in it. What is so strange about it that they call it magic or fabrication? It is not something bizarre.

﴿Say: I am not something new among the messengers. I do not know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am only a plain warner.﴾ (46:9) Say to them: "I am not some unprecedented messenger. I do not know what will happen to me tomorrow or to you. I only follow the revelation that is sent to me, and I am a clear warner."

The Prophet ﷺ was not the first messenger. Many messengers had passed before him. His case is like theirs. They had made no such claim. Many human beings were sent as messengers before. Allah knows who is fit for prophethood, and He gives them this office, and then they begin preaching without any deficiency or addition. This is the reality and nature of prophethood. When a messenger has been connected with the source of prophethood, he no longer asks Allah for any proof of his prophethood, nor does he ask for any special privilege for himself. As soon as the message comes, he begins his work. He begins to convey whatever reaches him.

﴿I do not know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me.﴾ (46:9) A messenger begins the work of prophethood not because he knows the unseen, or because he knows what the end will be for himself, his people, or his call. He acts according to Allah's signs and guidance. He has great trust in Allah, he is subject to Allah's will, and he acts according to Allah's instructions. He has great trust in Allah, he is subject to Allah's will, and he acts upon Allah's instructions. He takes every step by Allah's command, yet the future is not known to him. All secrets are with Allah, and the messenger is not restless to learn the secrets of the future, because his heart is at peace. Among the etiquettes of standing before the Lord of Glory is that one should be content with the knowledge that has been given to him and should not try to peer behind the veils of the future. The messenger always stands within the limits of his duties.

﴿I am only a plain warner.﴾ (46:9) These are the etiquettes of those who reach the court of Allah, and this is the tranquility of those who know Allah. They follow the example of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and continue to call people, not because they see the outcome of the call, and not because the future of the call is bright, or because they gain some small or great success as a result. They do this only because it is their duty, and nothing more. They do not ask their Lord for any proof, because the proof is in their hearts. They also do not ask Allah for any concessions. What greater favour or honour could there be than that they have been chosen for this work? They do not advance even the width of a hair beyond the fine line drawn for them, and they place their feet only on the footprints drawn for them.

After this, their attention is drawn to a close testimony. This testimony is that of the People of the Book, who are well acquainted with the descent of revelation.

﴿Say: Have you considered, if this is from Allah and you have disbelieved in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to something similar and believed while you remained arrogant? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (46:10) Say to them: "Have you ever considered: if this speech is from Allah and you have rejected it [what will your end be]? A witness from the Children of Israel has already borne testimony to a similar scripture. He believed, and you remained in your pride. Allah does not guide such wrongdoers."

It is possible that this refers to an event in which a person or a group from the Children of Israel, seeing that Quranic teachings resemble the Torah and other books, believed, because those who believed in the heavenly scriptures knew that this book says what is in those books. Some narrations state that this verse was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Salam, but what stands in the way of this is that he became a Muslim in Medina, and this surah is Meccan. There are also narrations that this verse is Medinan, because it was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Salam, while there are also narrations that it is Meccan and has no connection with the event of Abdullah ibn Salam.

It is also possible that it points to an event in Mecca, in which someone from the People of the Book believed, although the People of the Book were very few there. In Meccan circumstances, their belief would have had great importance, because the polytheists were unlettered, and in such a society the belief of People of the Book carried weight. This is why the Qur'an pointed to the testimony of the People of the Book in several places, and presented it to refute the polytheists who denied the Qur'an without proof, without evidence, without knowledge and skill, and without any book or heavenly tradition.

But the point to understand here is that the Qur'an has employed a hypothetical mode of argument here: "Have you considered that if this is from Allah and…" The purpose of this style of argument is to create wavering in the insistence of the polytheists, to reduce the intensity of their insistence, to cool their hostility, and to create in them some fear and caution, so that they do not advance so far in denial. And the argument is made that although you do not accept it, if it turns out to be true, then your end will be very bad. Therefore, keeping this supposition and possibility in view, be cautious: if this turns out to be true, all those punishments with which Muhammad ﷺ warns you will come upon you. So pause before denying the Messenger ﷺ, and reflect on this call, before you fall into such a dangerous end or before the possibility of such an end arises, especially in circumstances where a person or group from the Children of Israel has already given testimony that the nature of this book is like the speech of Allah, and on that basis believed. And when this book came first to you, in your language, through a man of your own, you are proud and deny it. This is clear injustice. It is abandoning clear truth and going forward, and in that case all your deeds will be lost and the punishment of Allah will come.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (46:10) In short, the Qur'an adopts every method to make people understand. It employs various styles of speech so that it may remove the doubts in human hearts, and it strives to convey its call to people's hearts through different paths. The various styles the Qur'an has adopted contain lessons and guidance for the callers who come later. Although for both Allah and His Messenger ﷺ the Qur'an was certainly the truth, the word of Allah, and there was no matter of doubt or possibility in it, yet this style was also adopted to make people understand, so that perhaps in this way the intensity of opposition might decrease.

The discussion then continues regarding what they used to say about the Qur'an, Islam, and the Islamic system, and an examination of it. They also used to put forward another justification for their denial and disbelief. This is the talk of the arrogant and those who consider themselves to be of high rank.

﴿And those who disbelieved say to those who believed: If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it. And since they have not been guided by it, they will surely say: This is an ancient falsehood.﴾ (46:11) "Those who have refused to accept say about the believers: If accepting this book were a good thing, these people would not have outstripped us in it. Since they were not guided by it, they will surely say: This is an ancient lie."

In the early days of Islam, the poor and the slaves rushed toward Islam. Therefore the great and the arrogant did not regard it favourably. This stuck in their eyes, and they used to say: If this religion were a good religion, would these people have known more and been more shrewd than us? They could not have preceded us in it, because we have more knowledge than them, we are more aware, and we have greater discernment between good and bad.

But the matter was not like this. The reason these great ones did not accept Islam was not that they doubted it, or that they were ignorant and did not know that the Noble Qur'an is pure truth, or that it contains no news. Rather, out of arrogance they acted this way, and they regarded accepting the truth as a task beneath them. Then they thought that in the present social order they would not retain the status they enjoyed in society, and the interests they possessed would not remain. Another reason was that regarding the ways of their forefathers they thought that this was a matter worthy of pride, whereas for those who rushed toward Islam at its first call, these obstacles did not exist that had stopped the great ones.

It is always the case that great people do not accept the truth. Because of pride and arrogance it is not possible for them to bow before the truth. Therefore they do not respond to the voice of nature, and they do not accept the proof. This pride and arrogance dictates to them that they should be stubborn and not accept it. They fabricate false excuses and make the falsest of false claims. Such great people never admit their mistakes. They are concerned with making their own selves the axis of life, and they want to continue as they are the axis in their present society.

﴿And since they have not been guided by it, they will surely say: This is an ancient falsehood.﴾ (46:11) Yes, if these people did not accept guidance, then necessarily there must be some defect in the truth. For great people cannot make mistakes! But these people presented themselves, in their own eyes and in the eyes of the common masses, as a kind of innocent creature free from error.

In any case, the passage on revelation and this study journey end with a reference to the Book of Moses, that the Qur'an is a link in the chain of earlier heavenly scriptures. Especially the Torah and the Qur'an have a deep resemblance, because the mission of Jesus (peace be upon him) was a completion of the Torah itself. Earlier, a reference was also made to a witness from the Children of Israel.

﴿And before it was the Book of Moses as a guide and mercy. And this is a Book confirming it in the Arabic tongue, to warn those who wronged and as good tidings to the doers of good.﴾ (46:12) "Before this, the Book of Moses came as a guide and mercy, and this Book, which confirms it, has come in the Arabic language, to warn the wrongdoers and to give good news to those who adopt a righteous course."

The Qur'an has repeatedly pointed to its relationship with the earlier heavenly scriptures, especially the Torah, because the book of Jesus was its completion and his mission was a continuation of the Torah. The original law was in the Torah itself. This is why it was given the title of imam and mercy, whereas every messengership is a mercy for this earth and its inhabitants, in this world and in the Hereafter.

﴿And this is a Book confirming it in the Arabic tongue.﴾ (46:12) This confirms the original books and original teachings on which all heavenly religions rest. This book confirms the system according to which all people of religion have walked. And this book confirms the straight path that leads human beings to Allah.

The phrase "in the Arabic tongue" was said here so that the favour bestowed upon the Arabs would be made manifest: that this book was sent down in their language. They were reminded that Allah had shown them special grace and particular kindness, in making them the bearers of this call and in granting their language the honour that the mighty Qur'an was revealed in it. The purpose was not language alone, but this.

﴿To warn those who wronged and as good tidings to the doers of good.﴾ (46:12) "So that it may warn the wrongdoers and give good tidings to those who do good."

At the end of this first lesson, a picture is drawn of the reward of the doers of good, and it is shown that the Noble Qur'an brings you this good news, provided they proclaim absolute monotheism and the lordship of Allah, then remain firm upon it and fulfil its requirements.

I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am only a clear warner." Say: "Have you considered, if it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to something like it and believed while you are arrogant? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people." Those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it." And since they have not been guided by it, they will surely say, "This is an ancient falsehood." And before it was the Book of Moses, a guide and a mercy. And this is a confirming Book in Arabic, to warn those who wronged and as good tidings to the doers of good﴾ (46:7–12).

The Qur'an's verses and its call are such that there is no doubt about them. They are very clear, appealing and manifest statements. Yet these people are so base, obstinate and wretched that they make this comment about the truth:

﴿This is obvious magic﴾ (46:7). "This is evident magic." But the Islamic call and magic differ in their nature and their subject matter. The aims of a prophet and of a sorcerer are entirely different. In this way, their wrong position is attacked, a position for which they have neither proof nor a valid answer, because the call of the Prophet (ﷺ) is very clear and consists of manifest signs.

Next, their other objection is taken up, which they used to raise: that this Qur'an is fabricated by Muhammad (ﷺ) himself, that it is attributed to Allah, and that it is a fabrication. The Qur'an presents this doubt in the form of a question: is this even a question at all? Could any reasonable person think such a thing?

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ (46:8). "Or do they say that he has invented it?" That is, have they become so audacious that they make such a statement, when even the thought of it cannot be conceived?

The Prophet (ﷺ) is told to answer this question in the manner befitting a prophet, because this question is very senseless. Through this answer, it should become apparent that he is well aware of his duties, that he is well aware of his Lord, and that he fully appreciates the true values and true powers of this universe.

﴿Say: "If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me against Allah at all. He is most knowing of what you say about it. Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful"﴾ (46:8). "Say: If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me against Allah at all. He knows best what you say about it. He is sufficient as a witness between me and you, and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful." Say to them: why would I invent a lie? For whose benefit would I invent it? For what aims would I do so? Is it so that you may believe in me and obey me? But what help can you give me?

﴿If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me against Allah at all﴾ (46:8). "If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me in any way against Allah." Because of my fabrication, He will certainly call me to account. Therefore, if you are with me and believe in me, what benefit would that be to me? When Allah calls me to account for the fabrication, what could you do at that time? You are very helpless and weak. What help could you give me?

This is an answer that befits a prophet, one who takes guidance from Allah and in whose sight nothing in this universe is visible except Allah. He sees only the power of Allah. It is also a logical and reasonable refutation, if anyone uses his intellect. By answering them, the Prophet (ﷺ) adds this:

﴿He is most knowing of what you say about it﴾ (46:8). "He knows best what you say about it." That is, what you do and say. And for those things that Allah knows, He will certainly punish you.

﴿Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you﴾ (46:8). "He is sufficient as a witness between me and you." Allah will both bear witness and make the decision, and the witness and judgment of Allah are sufficient.

﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ (46:8). "And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful." He is merciful to you, and through His mercy He guides you, and He forgives the errors you have committed, since previous deeds are pardoned after faith.

This refutation contains both a threat and a warning for them, and also an encouragement and an inducement to faith. In every way, Allah's effort is to change human hearts. The very fibre of the human being is touched, in the hope that the melody of faith may emerge. The listeners are given the impression that this matter is very important, and that the foolish things these people say are merely childish talk, mere claims they keep making. The message in the heart of the Great Caller, the thing to which he invites, is very great, while these people have no awareness of its importance and greatness.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 46, verses 4–12 (part 2 of 2):

Another angle is also used to answer their objection to revelation. Revelation is an event for which there are examples in history, and millions of people believe in it. What is so strange about it that they call it magic or fabrication? It is not something bizarre.

﴿Say: I am not something new among the messengers. I do not know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am only a plain warner.﴾ (46:9) Say to them: "I am not some unprecedented messenger. I do not know what will happen to me tomorrow or to you. I only follow the revelation that is sent to me, and I am a clear warner."

The Prophet ﷺ was not the first messenger. Many messengers had passed before him. His case is like theirs. They had made no such claim. Many human beings were sent as messengers before. Allah knows who is fit for prophethood, and He gives them this office, and then they begin preaching without any deficiency or addition. This is the reality and nature of prophethood. When a messenger has been connected with the source of prophethood, he no longer asks Allah for any proof of his prophethood, nor does he ask for any special privilege for himself. As soon as the message comes, he begins his work. He begins to convey whatever reaches him.

﴿I do not know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me.﴾ (46:9) A messenger begins the work of prophethood not because he knows the unseen, or because he knows what the end will be for himself, his people, or his call. He acts according to Allah's signs and guidance. He has great trust in Allah, he is subject to Allah's will, and he acts according to Allah's instructions. He has great trust in Allah, he is subject to Allah's will, and he acts upon Allah's instructions. He takes every step by Allah's command, yet the future is not known to him. All secrets are with Allah, and the messenger is not restless to learn the secrets of the future, because his heart is at peace. Among the etiquettes of standing before the Lord of Glory is that one should be content with the knowledge that has been given to him and should not try to peer behind the veils of the future. The messenger always stands within the limits of his duties.

﴿I am only a plain warner.﴾ (46:9) These are the etiquettes of those who reach the court of Allah, and this is the tranquility of those who know Allah. They follow the example of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and continue to call people, not because they see the outcome of the call, and not because the future of the call is bright, or because they gain some small or great success as a result. They do this only because it is their duty, and nothing more. They do not ask their Lord for any proof, because the proof is in their hearts. They also do not ask Allah for any concessions. What greater favour or honour could there be than that they have been chosen for this work? They do not advance even the width of a hair beyond the fine line drawn for them, and they place their feet only on the footprints drawn for them.

After this, their attention is drawn to a close testimony. This testimony is that of the People of the Book, who are well acquainted with the descent of revelation.

﴿Say: Have you considered, if this is from Allah and you have disbelieved in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to something similar and believed while you remained arrogant? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (46:10) Say to them: "Have you ever considered: if this speech is from Allah and you have rejected it [what will your end be]? A witness from the Children of Israel has already borne testimony to a similar scripture. He believed, and you remained in your pride. Allah does not guide such wrongdoers."

It is possible that this refers to an event in which a person or a group from the Children of Israel, seeing that Quranic teachings resemble the Torah and other books, believed, because those who believed in the heavenly scriptures knew that this book says what is in those books. Some narrations state that this verse was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Salam, but what stands in the way of this is that he became a Muslim in Medina, and this surah is Meccan. There are also narrations that this verse is Medinan, because it was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Salam, while there are also narrations that it is Meccan and has no connection with the event of Abdullah ibn Salam.

It is also possible that it points to an event in Mecca, in which someone from the People of the Book believed, although the People of the Book were very few there. In Meccan circumstances, their belief would have had great importance, because the polytheists were unlettered, and in such a society the belief of People of the Book carried weight. This is why the Qur'an pointed to the testimony of the People of the Book in several places, and presented it to refute the polytheists who denied the Qur'an without proof, without evidence, without knowledge and skill, and without any book or heavenly tradition.

But the point to understand here is that the Qur'an has employed a hypothetical mode of argument here: "Have you considered that if this is from Allah and…" The purpose of this style of argument is to create wavering in the insistence of the polytheists, to reduce the intensity of their insistence, to cool their hostility, and to create in them some fear and caution, so that they do not advance so far in denial. And the argument is made that although you do not accept it, if it turns out to be true, then your end will be very bad. Therefore, keeping this supposition and possibility in view, be cautious: if this turns out to be true, all those punishments with which Muhammad ﷺ warns you will come upon you. So pause before denying the Messenger ﷺ, and reflect on this call, before you fall into such a dangerous end or before the possibility of such an end arises, especially in circumstances where a person or group from the Children of Israel has already given testimony that the nature of this book is like the speech of Allah, and on that basis believed. And when this book came first to you, in your language, through a man of your own, you are proud and deny it. This is clear injustice. It is abandoning clear truth and going forward, and in that case all your deeds will be lost and the punishment of Allah will come.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (46:10) In short, the Qur'an adopts every method to make people understand. It employs various styles of speech so that it may remove the doubts in human hearts, and it strives to convey its call to people's hearts through different paths. The various styles the Qur'an has adopted contain lessons and guidance for the callers who come later. Although for both Allah and His Messenger ﷺ the Qur'an was certainly the truth, the word of Allah, and there was no matter of doubt or possibility in it, yet this style was also adopted to make people understand, so that perhaps in this way the intensity of opposition might decrease.

The discussion then continues regarding what they used to say about the Qur'an, Islam, and the Islamic system, and an examination of it. They also used to put forward another justification for their denial and disbelief. This is the talk of the arrogant and those who consider themselves to be of high rank.

﴿And those who disbelieved say to those who believed: If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it. And since they have not been guided by it, they will surely say: This is an ancient falsehood.﴾ (46:11) "Those who have refused to accept say about the believers: If accepting this book were a good thing, these people would not have outstripped us in it. Since they were not guided by it, they will surely say: This is an ancient lie."

In the early days of Islam, the poor and the slaves rushed toward Islam. Therefore the great and the arrogant did not regard it favourably. This stuck in their eyes, and they used to say: If this religion were a good religion, would these people have known more and been more shrewd than us? They could not have preceded us in it, because we have more knowledge than them, we are more aware, and we have greater discernment between good and bad.

But the matter was not like this. The reason these great ones did not accept Islam was not that they doubted it, or that they were ignorant and did not know that the Noble Qur'an is pure truth, or that it contains no news. Rather, out of arrogance they acted this way, and they regarded accepting the truth as a task beneath them. Then they thought that in the present social order they would not retain the status they enjoyed in society, and the interests they possessed would not remain. Another reason was that regarding the ways of their forefathers they thought that this was a matter worthy of pride, whereas for those who rushed toward Islam at its first call, these obstacles did not exist that had stopped the great ones.

It is always the case that great people do not accept the truth. Because of pride and arrogance it is not possible for them to bow before the truth. Therefore they do not respond to the voice of nature, and they do not accept the proof. This pride and arrogance dictates to them that they should be stubborn and not accept it. They fabricate false excuses and make the falsest of false claims. Such great people never admit their mistakes. They are concerned with making their own selves the axis of life, and they want to continue as they are the axis in their present society.

﴿And since they have not been guided by it, they will surely say: This is an ancient falsehood.﴾ (46:11) Yes, if these people did not accept guidance, then necessarily there must be some defect in the truth. For great people cannot make mistakes! But these people presented themselves, in their own eyes and in the eyes of the common masses, as a kind of innocent creature free from error.

In any case, the passage on revelation and this study journey end with a reference to the Book of Moses, that the Qur'an is a link in the chain of earlier heavenly scriptures. Especially the Torah and the Qur'an have a deep resemblance, because the mission of Jesus (peace be upon him) was a completion of the Torah itself. Earlier, a reference was also made to a witness from the Children of Israel.

﴿And before it was the Book of Moses as a guide and mercy. And this is a Book confirming it in the Arabic tongue, to warn those who wronged and as good tidings to the doers of good.﴾ (46:12) "Before this, the Book of Moses came as a guide and mercy, and this Book, which confirms it, has come in the Arabic language, to warn the wrongdoers and to give good news to those who adopt a righteous course."

The Qur'an has repeatedly pointed to its relationship with the earlier heavenly scriptures, especially the Torah, because the book of Jesus was its completion and his mission was a continuation of the Torah. The original law was in the Torah itself. This is why it was given the title of imam and mercy, whereas every messengership is a mercy for this earth and its inhabitants, in this world and in the Hereafter.

﴿And this is a Book confirming it in the Arabic tongue.﴾ (46:12) This confirms the original books and original teachings on which all heavenly religions rest. This book confirms the system according to which all people of religion have walked. And this book confirms the straight path that leads human beings to Allah.

The phrase "in the Arabic tongue" was said here so that the favour bestowed upon the Arabs would be made manifest: that this book was sent down in their language. They were reminded that Allah had shown them special grace and particular kindness, in making them the bearers of this call and in granting their language the honour that the mighty Qur'an was revealed in it. The purpose was not language alone, but this.

﴿To warn those who wronged and as good tidings to the doers of good.﴾ (46:12) "So that it may warn the wrongdoers and give good tidings to those who do good."

At the end of this first lesson, a picture is drawn of the reward of the doers of good, and it is shown that the Noble Qur'an brings you this good news, provided they proclaim absolute monotheism and the lordship of Allah, then remain firm upon it and fulfil its requirements.

Verses 4 to 12

Allah instructs the Prophet (ﷺ) to present to his people this cosmic testimony. The universe is an open book. Argument and debate cannot be conducted against this book, because it lies before everyone. It addresses human nature, and its logic and manner of speech are also natural. There is a deep connection between this book of the universe and the human nature. It cannot be suppressed, and no one can deceive anyone through it. This is a natural question:

﴿Show me what it is that they have created from the earth﴾ (46:4). "Show me, then, what they have created in the earth." It was not possible, and it is still not possible, that any of these man-made gods, whether stones, trees, jinn or angels, has created any part or thing of the earth. Natural reasoning, the reality of the matter, and every thing itself cry out that there is nothing. They have not created anything at all.

﴿Or do they have a share in the heavens?﴾ (46:4) "Or do they have any share in the heavens?" No person can even claim that the aforementioned gods have any share or partnership in the heavens. Even a superficial glance at the heavens shows how great the Creator of the universe is, and that He is One. In a single look, a reasonable person casts aside all misguidance and all the false gods. Allah, who is the Creator of man, knows that a deep contemplation of this universe alone transforms a human being. Therefore Allah repeatedly draws man's attention: cast a glance upon this open book of the universe, reflect upon its order, and ask the signals that come to your heart and mind from this universe what testimony they give.

After this, a question is posed in order to close the path of some extremely misguided people and to establish the proof against them. Sometimes, advancing further in misguidance, someone may boast that he has a counterfeit proof for his shirk, or may make some other excuse, although in reality he has no proof or argument. Therefore the Qur'an, before such people can speak, makes its demand: bring forth your proof, if you have any. The Qur'an also teaches them the method of reasoning, that is, what the correct procedure is for arriving at a decision.

﴿Bring me a Book before this, or any remnant of knowledge, if you are truthful﴾ (46:4). "Bring me a book that came before this one, or any remnant of knowledge that you have, if you are truthful." Either present a true book of Allah, or bring any trace that remains of the heavenly scriptures. All the heavenly books revealed before the Qur'an bear witness in support of the Qur'an that Allah alone is the Creator, that He alone is the Manager of the universe, and that He creates all things in a measured and proper manner. None of these books accepts the fables of multiple gods. Nor does any heavenly book contain any knowledge, influence or text stating that any of these gods created any part of the heavens or the earth, or had any share in creating anything.

The Qur'an also presents before them the testimony of the universe itself. The testimony of the universe is decisive testimony. In this way the Qur'an deprives their beliefs of any argument or proof, and also teaches them what the correct manner of debate and reasoning is. All these matters are taught in a single verse, whose words are few but forceful and decisive.

After this, the Qur'an presents to them the point that those things which you make into gods and then call upon are in reality without any substance. They do not even hear your call. Even if you call upon them throughout your lives in this world, and on the Day of Judgment, they will clearly deny you. Therefore, reflect upon this conduct of yours.

﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon, besides Allah, those who will not answer him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are heedless of their calling? And when mankind is gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ (46:5–6). "Who is more astray than the one who calls upon, besides Allah, those who cannot respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are even unaware of the calls of those who call upon them? And when mankind is gathered, these gods will become enemies to their worshippers and will deny their worship."

Some people regarded idols as deities in themselves. Some regarded them as deities, considering them to be likenesses of angels or righteous people. Some regarded trees as deities, and some regarded angels and Satan as deities. None of these could respond to the one who called upon them, or, if they heard the call, they could not benefit him. Stones and trees could neither hear nor respond. The angels also gave no answer to this conduct of the polytheists. As for the devils, they continued to whisper suggestions in order to lead them further astray. When the Day of Judgment comes and people are raised, all these gods that were worshipped will deny the worship of their misguided devotees. So much so that Satan, whose very work is to misguide people, will say:

﴿And when the matter has been decided, Satan will say: "Indeed, Allah promised you a true promise, and I promised you, but I failed you. I had no authority over you, except that I called you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I deny your association of me with Allah before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment"﴾ (14:22).

In this way the Qur'an presents them before their own claims and their own ideas, showing what the outcome of these claims will be in this world and in the Hereafter. Earlier they were shown the signs of the universe, which deny the beliefs of shirk. In both cases, what is established is that the only God of this universe is the Lord of the worlds, and that the very good of the polytheists themselves, in this world and in the Hereafter, lies in their reconsidering these ideas.

Here the Qur'an criticises those idolaters who were calling upon idols that could neither benefit nor harm them. At the time of the revelation of the Qur'an, such traditional living and dead deities existed. But this verse is not limited to those idols, which were called upon in a particular time and place, in a particular form, and upon which hopes were placed. The verse is very broad, and it includes all the deities besides Allah that will exist in any time or place: those whom the common people call upon, on whom they place their hopes, and who can bring them no benefit or harm, because the one who brings benefit and harm is Allah alone. In short, shirk is not limited to the simple form that existed among the Arabs at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an. There are many people who associate with Allah those in positions of authority. They associate officials, and they associate great capitalists. They place their hopes in them, call upon them, and yet all of them are extremely helpless and weak, and they cannot give any benefit. They do not even possess power over their own benefit and harm. To call upon such people is shirk, to place hopes in them is shirk, and to fear them is shirk. However, this shirk is a hidden shirk, and most people fall into it unconsciously.
