After this, their attention is drawn to a close testimony. This testimony is that of the People of the Book, who are well acquainted with the descent of revelation.

﴿Say: Have you considered, if this is from Allah and you have disbelieved in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to something similar and believed while you remained arrogant? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (46:10) Say to them: "Have you ever considered: if this speech is from Allah and you have rejected it [what will your end be]? A witness from the Children of Israel has already borne testimony to a similar scripture. He believed, and you remained in your pride. Allah does not guide such wrongdoers."

It is possible that this refers to an event in which a person or a group from the Children of Israel, seeing that Quranic teachings resemble the Torah and other books, believed, because those who believed in the heavenly scriptures knew that this book says what is in those books. Some narrations state that this verse was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Salam, but what stands in the way of this is that he became a Muslim in Medina, and this surah is Meccan. There are also narrations that this verse is Medinan, because it was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Salam, while there are also narrations that it is Meccan and has no connection with the event of Abdullah ibn Salam.

It is also possible that it points to an event in Mecca, in which someone from the People of the Book believed, although the People of the Book were very few there. In Meccan circumstances, their belief would have had great importance, because the polytheists were unlettered, and in such a society the belief of People of the Book carried weight. This is why the Qur'an pointed to the testimony of the People of the Book in several places, and presented it to refute the polytheists who denied the Qur'an without proof, without evidence, without knowledge and skill, and without any book or heavenly tradition.

But the point to understand here is that the Qur'an has employed a hypothetical mode of argument here: "Have you considered that if this is from Allah and…" The purpose of this style of argument is to create wavering in the insistence of the polytheists, to reduce the intensity of their insistence, to cool their hostility, and to create in them some fear and caution, so that they do not advance so far in denial. And the argument is made that although you do not accept it, if it turns out to be true, then your end will be very bad. Therefore, keeping this supposition and possibility in view, be cautious: if this turns out to be true, all those punishments with which Muhammad ﷺ warns you will come upon you. So pause before denying the Messenger ﷺ, and reflect on this call, before you fall into such a dangerous end or before the possibility of such an end arises, especially in circumstances where a person or group from the Children of Israel has already given testimony that the nature of this book is like the speech of Allah, and on that basis believed. And when this book came first to you, in your language, through a man of your own, you are proud and deny it. This is clear injustice. It is abandoning clear truth and going forward, and in that case all your deeds will be lost and the punishment of Allah will come.

﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (46:10) In short, the Qur'an adopts every method to make people understand. It employs various styles of speech so that it may remove the doubts in human hearts, and it strives to convey its call to people's hearts through different paths. The various styles the Qur'an has adopted contain lessons and guidance for the callers who come later. Although for both Allah and His Messenger ﷺ the Qur'an was certainly the truth, the word of Allah, and there was no matter of doubt or possibility in it, yet this style was also adopted to make people understand, so that perhaps in this way the intensity of opposition might decrease.

The discussion then continues regarding what they used to say about the Qur'an, Islam, and the Islamic system, and an examination of it. They also used to put forward another justification for their denial and disbelief. This is the talk of the arrogant and those who consider themselves to be of high rank.

﴿And those who disbelieved say to those who believed: If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it. And since they have not been guided by it, they will surely say: This is an ancient falsehood.﴾ (46:11) "Those who have refused to accept say about the believers: If accepting this book were a good thing, these people would not have outstripped us in it. Since they were not guided by it, they will surely say: This is an ancient lie."

In the early days of Islam, the poor and the slaves rushed toward Islam. Therefore the great and the arrogant did not regard it favourably. This stuck in their eyes, and they used to say: If this religion were a good religion, would these people have known more and been more shrewd than us? They could not have preceded us in it, because we have more knowledge than them, we are more aware, and we have greater discernment between good and bad.

But the matter was not like this. The reason these great ones did not accept Islam was not that they doubted it, or that they were ignorant and did not know that the Noble Qur'an is pure truth, or that it contains no news. Rather, out of arrogance they acted this way, and they regarded accepting the truth as a task beneath them. Then they thought that in the present social order they would not retain the status they enjoyed in society, and the interests they possessed would not remain. Another reason was that regarding the ways of their forefathers they thought that this was a matter worthy of pride, whereas for those who rushed toward Islam at its first call, these obstacles did not exist that had stopped the great ones.

It is always the case that great people do not accept the truth. Because of pride and arrogance it is not possible for them to bow before the truth. Therefore they do not respond to the voice of nature, and they do not accept the proof. This pride and arrogance dictates to them that they should be stubborn and not accept it. They fabricate false excuses and make the falsest of false claims. Such great people never admit their mistakes. They are concerned with making their own selves the axis of life, and they want to continue as they are the axis in their present society.

﴿And since they have not been guided by it, they will surely say: This is an ancient falsehood.﴾ (46:11) Yes, if these people did not accept guidance, then necessarily there must be some defect in the truth. For great people cannot make mistakes! But these people presented themselves, in their own eyes and in the eyes of the common masses, as a kind of innocent creature free from error.

In any case, the passage on revelation and this study journey end with a reference to the Book of Moses, that the Qur'an is a link in the chain of earlier heavenly scriptures. Especially the Torah and the Qur'an have a deep resemblance, because the mission of Jesus (peace be upon him) was a completion of the Torah itself. Earlier, a reference was also made to a witness from the Children of Israel.

﴿And before it was the Book of Moses as a guide and mercy. And this is a Book confirming it in the Arabic tongue, to warn those who wronged and as good tidings to the doers of good.﴾ (46:12) "Before this, the Book of Moses came as a guide and mercy, and this Book, which confirms it, has come in the Arabic language, to warn the wrongdoers and to give good news to those who adopt a righteous course."

The Qur'an has repeatedly pointed to its relationship with the earlier heavenly scriptures, especially the Torah, because the book of Jesus was its completion and his mission was a continuation of the Torah. The original law was in the Torah itself. This is why it was given the title of imam and mercy, whereas every messengership is a mercy for this earth and its inhabitants, in this world and in the Hereafter.

﴿And this is a Book confirming it in the Arabic tongue.﴾ (46:12) This confirms the original books and original teachings on which all heavenly religions rest. This book confirms the system according to which all people of religion have walked. And this book confirms the straight path that leads human beings to Allah.

The phrase "in the Arabic tongue" was said here so that the favour bestowed upon the Arabs would be made manifest: that this book was sent down in their language. They were reminded that Allah had shown them special grace and particular kindness, in making them the bearers of this call and in granting their language the honour that the mighty Qur'an was revealed in it. The purpose was not language alone, but this.

﴿To warn those who wronged and as good tidings to the doers of good.﴾ (46:12) "So that it may warn the wrongdoers and give good tidings to those who do good."

At the end of this first lesson, a picture is drawn of the reward of the doers of good, and it is shown that the Noble Qur'an brings you this good news, provided they proclaim absolute monotheism and the lordship of Allah, then remain firm upon it and fulfil its requirements.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah 46, verses 4–12 (part 1 of 2)**

Verses 4 to 12

Allah instructs the Prophet (ﷺ) to present to his people this cosmic testimony. The universe is an open book. Argument and debate cannot be conducted against this book, because it lies before everyone. It addresses human nature, and its logic and manner of speech are also natural. There is a deep connection between this book of the universe and the human nature. It cannot be suppressed, and no one can deceive anyone through it. This is a natural question:

﴿Show me what it is that they have created from the earth﴾ (46:4). "Show me, then, what they have created in the earth." It was not possible, and it is still not possible, that any of these man-made gods, whether stones, trees, jinn or angels, has created any part or thing of the earth. Natural reasoning, the reality of the matter, and every thing itself cry out that there is nothing. They have not created anything at all.

﴿Or do they have a share in the heavens?﴾ (46:4) "Or do they have any share in the heavens?" No person can even claim that the aforementioned gods have any share or partnership in the heavens. Even a superficial glance at the heavens shows how great the Creator of the universe is, and that He is One. In a single look, a reasonable person casts aside all misguidance and all the false gods. Allah, who is the Creator of man, knows that a deep contemplation of this universe alone transforms a human being. Therefore Allah repeatedly draws man's attention: cast a glance upon this open book of the universe, reflect upon its order, and ask the signals that come to your heart and mind from this universe what testimony they give.

After this, a question is posed in order to close the path of some extremely misguided people and to establish the proof against them. Sometimes, advancing further in misguidance, someone may boast that he has a counterfeit proof for his shirk, or may make some other excuse, although in reality he has no proof or argument. Therefore the Qur'an, before such people can speak, makes its demand: bring forth your proof, if you have any. The Qur'an also teaches them the method of reasoning, that is, what the correct procedure is for arriving at a decision.

﴿Bring me a Book before this, or any remnant of knowledge, if you are truthful﴾ (46:4). "Bring me a book that came before this one, or any remnant of knowledge that you have, if you are truthful." Either present a true book of Allah, or bring any trace that remains of the heavenly scriptures. All the heavenly books revealed before the Qur'an bear witness in support of the Qur'an that Allah alone is the Creator, that He alone is the Manager of the universe, and that He creates all things in a measured and proper manner. None of these books accepts the fables of multiple gods. Nor does any heavenly book contain any knowledge, influence or text stating that any of these gods created any part of the heavens or the earth, or had any share in creating anything.

The Qur'an also presents before them the testimony of the universe itself. The testimony of the universe is decisive testimony. In this way the Qur'an deprives their beliefs of any argument or proof, and also teaches them what the correct manner of debate and reasoning is. All these matters are taught in a single verse, whose words are few but forceful and decisive.

After this, the Qur'an presents to them the point that those things which you make into gods and then call upon are in reality without any substance. They do not even hear your call. Even if you call upon them throughout your lives in this world, and on the Day of Judgment, they will clearly deny you. Therefore, reflect upon this conduct of yours.

﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon, besides Allah, those who will not answer him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are heedless of their calling? And when mankind is gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ (46:5–6). "Who is more astray than the one who calls upon, besides Allah, those who cannot respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are even unaware of the calls of those who call upon them? And when mankind is gathered, these gods will become enemies to their worshippers and will deny their worship."

Some people regarded idols as deities in themselves. Some regarded them as deities, considering them to be likenesses of angels or righteous people. Some regarded trees as deities, and some regarded angels and Satan as deities. None of these could respond to the one who called upon them, or, if they heard the call, they could not benefit him. Stones and trees could neither hear nor respond. The angels also gave no answer to this conduct of the polytheists. As for the devils, they continued to whisper suggestions in order to lead them further astray. When the Day of Judgment comes and people are raised, all these gods that were worshipped will deny the worship of their misguided devotees. So much so that Satan, whose very work is to misguide people, will say:

﴿And when the matter has been decided, Satan will say: "Indeed, Allah promised you a true promise, and I promised you, but I failed you. I had no authority over you, except that I called you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I deny your association of me with Allah before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment"﴾ (14:22).

In this way the Qur'an presents them before their own claims and their own ideas, showing what the outcome of these claims will be in this world and in the Hereafter. Earlier they were shown the signs of the universe, which deny the beliefs of shirk. In both cases, what is established is that the only God of this universe is the Lord of the worlds, and that the very good of the polytheists themselves, in this world and in the Hereafter, lies in their reconsidering these ideas.

Here the Qur'an criticises those idolaters who were calling upon idols that could neither benefit nor harm them. At the time of the revelation of the Qur'an, such traditional living and dead deities existed. But this verse is not limited to those idols, which were called upon in a particular time and place, in a particular form, and upon which hopes were placed. The verse is very broad, and it includes all the deities besides Allah that will exist in any time or place: those whom the common people call upon, on whom they place their hopes, and who can bring them no benefit or harm, because the one who brings benefit and harm is Allah alone. In short, shirk is not limited to the simple form that existed among the Arabs at the time of the revelation of the Qur'an. There are many people who associate with Allah those in positions of authority. They associate officials, and they associate great capitalists. They place their hopes in them, call upon them, and yet all of them are extremely helpless and weak, and they cannot give any benefit. They do not even possess power over their own benefit and harm. To call upon such people is shirk, to place hopes in them is shirk, and to fear them is shirk. However, this shirk is a hidden shirk, and most people fall into it unconsciously.

* * *

After this, a discussion takes place concerning the position of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his true call. Their ideas about shirk have been thoroughly examined. Now it is explained how wrong and unreasonable their position is regarding revelation and the Islamic call.

﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say of the truth when it comes to them, "This is obvious magic." Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say: "If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me against Allah at all. He is most knowing of what you say about it. Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful." Say: "I am not something new among the messengers, and I do not know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am only a clear warner." Say: "Have you considered, if it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to something like it and believed while you are arrogant? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people." Those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it." And since they have not been guided by it, they will surely say, "This is an ancient falsehood." And before it was the Book of Moses, a guide and a mercy. And this is a confirming Book in Arabic, to warn those who wronged and as good tidings to the doers of good﴾ (46:7–12).

The Qur'an's verses and its call are such that there is no doubt about them. They are very clear, appealing and manifest statements. Yet these people are so base, obstinate and wretched that they make this comment about the truth:

﴿This is obvious magic﴾ (46:7). "This is evident magic." But the Islamic call and magic differ in their nature and their subject matter. The aims of a prophet and of a sorcerer are entirely different. In this way, their wrong position is attacked, a position for which they have neither proof nor a valid answer, because the call of the Prophet (ﷺ) is very clear and consists of manifest signs.

Next, their other objection is taken up, which they used to raise: that this Qur'an is fabricated by Muhammad (ﷺ) himself, that it is attributed to Allah, and that it is a fabrication. The Qur'an presents this doubt in the form of a question: is this even a question at all? Could any reasonable person think such a thing?

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ (46:8). "Or do they say that he has invented it?" That is, have they become so audacious that they make such a statement, when even the thought of it cannot be conceived?

The Prophet (ﷺ) is told to answer this question in the manner befitting a prophet, because this question is very senseless. Through this answer, it should become apparent that he is well aware of his duties, that he is well aware of his Lord, and that he fully appreciates the true values and true powers of this universe.

﴿Say: "If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me against Allah at all. He is most knowing of what you say about it. Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful"﴾ (46:8). "Say: If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me against Allah at all. He knows best what you say about it. He is sufficient as a witness between me and you, and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful." Say to them: why would I invent a lie? For whose benefit would I invent it? For what aims would I do so? Is it so that you may believe in me and obey me? But what help can you give me?

﴿If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me against Allah at all﴾ (46:8). "If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me in any way against Allah." Because of my fabrication, He will certainly call me to account. Therefore, if you are with me and believe in me, what benefit would that be to me? When Allah calls me to account for the fabrication, what could you do at that time? You are very helpless and weak. What help could you give me?

This is an answer that befits a prophet, one who takes guidance from Allah and in whose sight nothing in this universe is visible except Allah. He sees only the power of Allah. It is also a logical and reasonable refutation, if anyone uses his intellect. By answering them, the Prophet (ﷺ) adds this:

﴿He is most knowing of what you say about it﴾ (46:8). "He knows best what you say about it." That is, what you do and say. And for those things that Allah knows, He will certainly punish you.

﴿Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you﴾ (46:8). "He is sufficient as a witness between me and you." Allah will both bear witness and make the decision, and the witness and judgment of Allah are sufficient.

﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ (46:8). "And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful." He is merciful to you, and through His mercy He guides you, and He forgives the errors you have committed, since previous deeds are pardoned after faith.

This refutation contains both a threat and a warning for them, and also an encouragement and an inducement to faith. In every way, Allah's effort is to change human hearts. The very fibre of the human being is touched, in the hope that the melody of faith may emerge. The listeners are given the impression that this matter is very important, and that the foolish things these people say are merely childish talk, mere claims they keep making. The message in the heart of the Great Caller, the thing to which he invites, is very great, while these people have no awareness of its importance and greatness.

﴿To warn those who wronged and as good tidings to the doers of good.﴾ (46:12) "So that it may warn the wrongdoers and give good tidings to those who do good."

At the end of this first lesson, a picture is drawn of the reward of the doers of good, and it is shown that the Noble Qur'an brings you this good news, provided they proclaim absolute monotheism and the lordship of Allah, then remain firm upon it and fulfil its requirements.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 46, verses 13–14:

Verses 13 to 14

That they said, "Our Lord is Allah." This is not an ordinary matter that they said. It is not merely a belief, but the affirmation of a complete system of life. "Our Lord is Allah" is the name of all the activities of life: Allah is our Lord in our thinking, in our views, in our deeds, and in our entire relationships in this world.

Allah is our Lord, therefore we shall worship Him alone, fear Him alone, place our trust in Him alone, and turn our faces toward Him alone. Allah is our Lord, therefore all resources and means belong to Him, no one else has any standing apart from Him, and no greed or desire for anyone else is lawful.

Allah is our Lord, therefore every activity, every thought, and every destiny is directed toward Him, and in everything His pleasure is sought. Allah is our Lord, therefore He alone will judge, the Shariah and the law will be His, and guidance and direction will come from Him. Allah is our Lord, therefore the people and things in this universe are connected with us and we have a relationship with them, because their Lord is also Allah. Allah is our Lord, so we shall also derive our system of life from Him. These will not be mere words, nor mere belief, but a divine system.

"Then they remained steadfast" (46:13): this is the second condition, namely that having accepted the Islamic system, they stood firm upon it. Their hearts and souls found contentment in it, their ideas and concepts became fixed upon it, every kind of restlessness and doubt came to an end, all other interests and all ... came to an end, and all inclinations and tendencies ceased. It should be remembered that worldly interests are varied and alluring, and to remain firm upon a system and method is a very difficult task. At every step there are places where people may slip and obstacles, and from every direction voices arise pulling them toward themselves.

After saying "Our Lord is Allah" (46:13), one must adopt the entire system of life and remain firmly upon it. Those whom Allah has granted recognition of the truth and steadfastness upon the truth are very great and chosen people, and it is they for whom this judgment was issued.

"There shall be no fear for them, nor shall they grieve" (46:13): why should they fear, and why should they be troubled? The system they have adopted leads to Allah, and remaining firm upon it is a guarantee from Allah.

"Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding therein forever, as a recompense for what they used to do" (46:14). Here the word "ya'malun" (they used to do) explains "Our Lord is Allah," and defines the meaning of steadfastness upon the path. The meaning is that abiding forever in Paradise is because of your deeds and your steadfastness. That is, action upon the method of "Allah is ours," and steady, continuous action upon it, becomes manifest, and they remain firm upon it.

This shows that in this religion, beliefs and concepts are not merely words, such that someone may just recite the words of the Kalimah Tayyibah, but the Kalimah Tayyibah is a way of life. If the Kalimah were merely words and did not become a way of life, it would not be the Kalimah of the pillars of Islam. Today millions of people bear witness to the Kalimah Tayyibah merely with their tongues, but this Kalimah does not go beyond their lips, it does not have any effect on their lives, and it does not bring about any change within them. After reciting the Kalimah they live the same ignorant (jahili) life that the idol-worshippers live, while with their lips they recite this Kalimah day and night; these are only words, and in their lives there is no meaning of it.

"La ilaha illa Allah," or "Ya Rabbana Allah," or "Allah is our Lord," or "There is no deity except Allah": in reality this is a way and method of living. Every Muslim should firmly fix this meaning in his mind, so that he then seeks out the system to which these words point, reflects upon that system, and is concerned to establish it.

Lesson No. 238: At a Glance

This lesson is about human nature: how a person behaves when he is upon sound fitra, and what his days and nights become when that nature is corrupted. It begins with the admonition to show good treatment to one's parents. In the Qur'an, the injunction concerning parents, especially, comes immediately after the affirmation of Islamic belief. This is because, after the bond of faith, Islam gives importance to good relations between parents and children. After faith, it is a believer's duty to treat his parents well. Why is good treatment of parents brought immediately after accepting Islam and adopting the belief in Tawhid? There are two reasons. One is that Islam gives great importance to honouring parents. The second is that Islam and the Qur'an wish to show that the bond between father and son is the strongest of bonds, yet the Islamic bond and brotherhood are superior even to blood relations.

Two examples are given in this lesson. One example is that between parents and children there is a blood relationship, and then there is also an ideological relationship. In that case the bond between the two will be a guided bond, and both will reach Allah and deserve Paradise. In the second example, the bond of lineage is separated from the bond of faith; they do not meet. In that case, despite the blood relationship, the offspring deserves Hell. Then one scene of the Day of Resurrection is also presented, in which the picture of depravity (fisq) and arrogance (istikbar) is drawn.

Lesson No. 238: Explanation of the Verses

15 to 20

Verses 15 to 16

This injunction is for the whole human species, and it rests upon the basis of humanity. For this injunction no quality other than being human has been required, and no condition or restriction has been attached to the kindness either. The mere fact of being a father makes it obligatory that kindness be shown to him; no other quality is necessary alongside fatherhood. This injunction was revealed by Allah, who is the Creator of man, and perhaps this injunction has been given only to man. Other categories of creation perhaps have not been given this command. Until today it has not been known that other animals, birds and creeping things have any such guidance. Yes, it is also seen in the nature of animals that they raise their young. Thus it appears that this injunction is only for man, and indeed it is a distinctive feature of man.

The command in the Qur'an has been repeated in the form of an injunction, and in the Hadith too it is strongly emphasised. However, parents are very rarely enjoined concerning their children; if there is any guidance, it concerns certain circumstances. The reason is that the nurturing of the child has been placed within the very nature of parents. Parents themselves advance towards raising the child, and in this matter there is no need to urge them to the task. Parents make such sacrifices for their children that sometimes they sacrifice even their lives for them. Sorrow and pain are a minor matter, and in this connection they do not seek any return from them, nor do they expect gratitude from them. But the young generation seldom looks back, because the demand for this kind of sacrifice is made by their own children, and thus the cart of life keeps moving along.

But Islam, in accordance with its natural teachings, has appointed the family as the first unit of society. The family is the cradle in which weak children are nurtured and grow up. From this cradle children acquire love, cooperation, mutual support, and the building and training of the family. A child who does not receive the training of a family is deficient in some aspect of his personality, even if outside the family circle he is provided with the necessities of life in abundance and a good arrangement has been made for his education and training. The greatest deficiency in such a child is a deficiency in the awareness of love. It has been established among scholars of psychology that every child wishes to remain in his mother's lap for the first two years of life, and he does not accept anyone else's participation in this. Among the artificial institutions for raising children that have been created in the world, the mother is above all absent, because the woman working there, that is the nurse, has to look after many children. Those children then develop jealousy towards one another, because they compete for the artificial shared mother; thus malice and enmity grow in them from their early life, and in that tender heart in which hatred has arisen, love is not later produced. Then a child needs, for a long time, one single supervision so that stability may come into his personality, and this can arise only within a family. As for the artificial institutions for raising children, in them the child is deprived of a single firm guardian, because the duty-shifts of the artificial mothers also keep changing. Therefore disorder exists within their personalities too, and they are deprived of a strong personality. From the experiments of such institutions that are coming to light, it is known that the family nursery which Islam has made essential for the raising of children contains deep wisdom, and that the natural method of child training is the one Islam has prescribed, which is free from every kind of defect.

And here the Qur'an records the role of the mother: the hardships of the mother, the loves of the mother, her struggle, and a most generous manner and noble conduct. Even if a child keeps busy day and night in fulfilling the command of Allah to show kindness to his parents, he still cannot repay the mother's kindness.

﴿His mother bore him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, and his carrying and weaning took thirty months﴾ (46:15).

The words that Allah has chosen for the hardships of the mother, their very pronunciation expresses hardship. Through the sound and cadence of the words, struggle, toil and fatigue are made apparent.

﴿His mother bore him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship﴾ (46:15). Just as a tired man takes long breaths, breathes with difficulty, and is exhausted, this is the picture of pregnancy, especially in its final days; and the difficulty of childbirth, its hardships and its pains are known to everyone.

Nowadays embryology has advanced greatly, and mankind has come to know all the stages of pregnancy and the processes occurring within it. From these it is known how much hardship the mother bears in all these processes, and how much sacrifice she gives... When the woman's ovum is joined by the sperm cell, it strives to cling to the walls of the womb, and as soon as it clings to the wall of the womb it begins to consume that wall, because it has the capacity to eat. Thus it begins to lick the walls of the womb like a termite. At the place where it begins to eat, the mother's blood gathers and a small pool is formed, and this ovum, within which is the cell, and these cells are in that pool of blood, and the blood contains the essence of the mother's body. It sucks this blood, grows, keeps licking the walls of the womb and keeps drinking blood, and obtains the essence of life. The mother eats food, drinks water, and after digesting the nourishment she produces fresh blood for that ovum and that cell, and supplies nourishment to that blood-devouring cell. A time comes when the bones of the child begin to form, and at that time it begins to suck even more blood. In such circumstances the mother sometimes requires calcium, because in this period the woman supplies the marrow of her bones to that child so that the child's bodily frame may be formed. This is only a small part of that great struggle. Then comes the stage of childbirth. This is an extremely laborious and agonising process. But because of the immense love that the mother has for her child, she bears all of this, since it is the demand of nature. Thus the mother gives life to that small child and herself is gradually melted away. After this comes the stage of nursing, and then of rearing and bringing up. After this she gives him, in the form of milk, the essence of her flesh and blood. And she raises him by expending the full strength of her heart, mind and nerves. Yet she accepts all these hardships gladly, with the utmost love and a merciful manner. She never tires, and never feels hatred towards the child. The reward for all these hardships, this mother wants only this: that her child be sound and whole and keep growing. This indeed is the reward she desires.

No one can give the mother a recompense for this long struggle, hardship and sacrifice. However much effort anyone makes in serving the mother, no one can give her its recompense. Even if someone makes great effort, that too will be small.

A man was circumambulating the Ka'bah carrying his mother on his back, and when he came before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ he said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have fulfilled her right." He ﷺ said: "No, not even equal to a single breath." (al-Bazzar)

Now the Qur'an, having led this human being through the injunction of kindness to parents and the stage of the mother's unparalleled hardships and sacrifices, brings him to the age of maturity. Now he is strong, vigorous and wise, his nature is right, and his heart is guided; and this is the human being the Qur'an desires.

﴿Until, when he reaches his full strength and reaches forty years, he says: "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favour which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteous deeds with which You are pleased, and make my offspring righteous for me. Indeed I have turned to You in repentance, and indeed I am of those who submit"﴾ (46:15).

Man reaches the age of maturity between twenty and forty. Forty years are the culmination of guidance and right direction; in this, all of a person's faculties are complete, and a person attains completeness in reflection and contemplation. Now he passes through the stages of completion, and stability arises within him. At this age, if he is of upright nature, he thinks a little above this life, and then he also reflects upon the end of all mankind.

The Qur'an records here the mental experience of a personality who possesses a sound nature, at the stage where a person has left a part of his life behind and, in the later years, turns again towards Allah, if he is of upright nature.

﴿My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favour which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents﴾ (46:15). This is the prayer of a heart that is conscious of its Lord's favours: that these are the bounties You bestowed upon me, and upon my parents before me, and that these bounties have continued from earlier times without interruption. In comparison with them, our capacity for gratitude is very small. O Allah, You Yourself grant us the ability and the self-control to be able to render this gratitude. Let it not be that I scatter myself here and there and waste my strength in disorder, and leave aside the real task, which is to render the gratitude due to Allah.

﴿And that I do righteous deeds with which You are pleased﴾ (46:15). This is the second prayer. This person seeks Allah's help so that he may be able to do righteous deeds. He wishes to employ his perfection and his goodness in the work of the pleasure of his Lord, since the pleasure of Allah is his great aim. For the attainment of the pleasure of Allah alone is his whole striving.

﴿And make my offspring righteous for me﴾ (46:15). This is the third prayer. Every righteous person has the desire that his righteousness be transmitted to his offspring, and that his heart be at peace knowing that among his descendants there are people who after him will seek the worship of Allah and His good pleasure. Righteous offspring is the first wish of a righteous servant, and compared with treasures and wealth he prefers righteous offspring. More than every adornment of life, he likes righteous offspring, and this prayer is moving from parents towards their offspring, that the worship of Allah may continue in the coming generations. And as for the petitions and requests that he is making, the intercession for their acceptance that he presents is this: "I repent and I bow my head in submission."

﴿Indeed I have turned to You in repentance, and indeed I am of those who submit﴾ (46:15). These are the attributes of a model righteous servant in relation to his Lord, whose nature is straight and sound. How Allah's relationship with such servants then is, the Qur'an has also explained.

* * * * *

﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did, and overlook their evil deeds; they will be among the companions of Paradise, a true promise which they were promised﴾ (46:16).

With Allah, reward is based upon good deeds, and sins are forgiven; and such people will join the true inhabitants of Paradise, and this is Allah's promise, which is a true promise. This promise was made in the world, and Allah never breaks His promise.

* * *

And in contrast to this good example, observe also the grief of depravity, immorality and misguidance.

**Lesson No. 239: An Overview**

This lesson takes up a subject entirely different from the previous two lessons. Where the earlier lessons addressed the human heart and vision from other angles, this one takes a new perspective. In it, the disbelievers of Makkah are taken on a tour of the valley of al-Ahqaf, and of the other communities that were destroyed, all of which lay around Makkah. These people were thoroughly aware of the events that befell the people of 'Ad and their prophet, Hud (peace be upon him). They too treated their prophet in the same way that these people are treating the Prophet ﷺ. They too raised the same objections that these people are raising. Hud (peace be upon him), within the bounds and limits of the manners of prophethood, gave them their answers. Yet the people of Makkah know what a severe punishment of Allah came upon them. Their strength could not withstand that punishment, even though they were physically stronger than the people of Makkah. Their wealth and affluence gave them no benefit, even though they were richer than them. They had eyes, ears, hearts and minds just like these people, but they did not benefit from them. Compared to them, they were also higher in intellect, and the gods they had made could not come to their aid.

In short, by setting the disbelievers of Makkah before the outcome of their own forefathers, the Qur'an presents their picture before them. It shows that the line of prophethood is one continuous lineage and tree, that there is one call, and that the divine way (Sunnat Ilahiyyah) is also one. They denied, and they were destroyed; you deny, and you make yourselves deserving of destruction. The doctrine of Tawhid is not a newly fabricated belief; this call has been running through history since the call of Nuh (peace be upon him). There is no difference in it due to differences of time and place.

**Lesson No. 239: Explanation of the Verses**

**Verses 21 to 28**

**Verses 21 to 28**

Al-Ahqaf is the plural of *hiqf*, which means a high sand dune. The dwellings of the people of 'Ad were on high dunes in the region of Hadramawt, to the south of the Arabian Peninsula.

The Noble Messenger ﷺ is commanded to narrate to these people the story of 'Ad, and to tell them that their brother Hud also warned his people in the same way. This is because the reaction of the people of 'Ad to the call of Hud (peace be upon him) was just like the way the Quraysh are denying the call of the Prophet ﷺ. Just as you are from among them, Hud was also from among 'Ad. But let these people take heed that denying the truth can have the same consequences. The land of 'Ad was near the Quraysh, and they were also aware of their events.

Hud (peace be upon him), the brother of 'Ad, warned his people. Hud was not the first of the messengers; many communities had received messengers before him.

﴿And warners had come before him and after him﴾ (46:21). Warners had come, both before him and after him, in regard to time and place, so they were both near and far from them. This is because Allah continued the sequence of warning people of the evil end for His creation, and the call and prophethood have continued since ancient times. This was not a strange or unusual matter.

﴿And warn them with that which all messengers warned with﴾. ﴿That you worship none but Allah; indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a great day﴾ (46:21). Worship Allah alone: that is, hold the belief of Tawhid, and also obey the commands of Allah throughout your whole life. If you oppose this call, you will be afflicted with the punishment of this world and the Hereafter. The reference is to the punishment of the Great Day. In the Qur'an, the term "Great Day" is applied to the Day of Resurrection, because the terrors of the Day of Resurrection are great and severe.

What was the outcome of this call to turn to Allah and of this warning of the punishment of Allah?

*****

﴿They said, "Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods? Then bring us what you threaten, if you are truthful"﴾ (46:22).

They had an ill opinion of their brother, and instead they challenged him in return: bring the punishment with which you threaten us. Along with this, they also mocked him and insisted on falsehood. Hud, like a prophet, bore all these things. He made no grand claims, and spoke within his limits.

*****

﴿He said, "Knowledge is only with Allah. I convey to you what I have been sent with, but I see that you are a people acting ignorantly"﴾ (46:23).

I only warn you of the punishment, because I have been commanded to warn you. I do not know when the punishment will come, nor what it will be like. Knowledge of these matters is with Allah. I am only a conveyor of the message from Allah. I do not share with Allah in knowledge or power.

﴿But I see you as a people acting ignorantly﴾ (46:23). You appear to be very foolish. What greater folly could there be than that a brother and a compassionate advisor is warning you, and in response you issue a challenge?

Between Hud (peace be upon him) and his people, there was a lengthy dialogue and debate concerning the Islamic call. Here the Qur'an condenses it, because here the outcome of their evil end must be presented in rapid succession, so that their challenge and haste may be answered.

*****

﴿Then, when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, "This is a cloud that will bring us rain." ... "No, rather it is that which you were impatient for: a wind in which is a painful punishment, destroying everything by the command of its Lord." So they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings. Thus do We recompense the criminal people﴾ (46:24-25).

It is narrated that severe heat seized them. The rain stopped, and due to the dryness and intense heat, the region became fire and smoke. After that, a piece of cloud came. These people were very pleased, and they went out into the valleys to welcome this cloud. They thought that now it would surely rain.

﴿They said, "This is a cloud that will bring us rain"﴾ (46:24).

And the state of affairs answered them:

﴿No, rather it is that which you were impatient for: a wind in which is a painful punishment, destroying everything by the command of its Lord﴾ (46:24-25). This is an extremely swift wind, and it is as harsh and uncontrollable as an arrogant tyrant.

﴿It left nothing that it came upon but made it like decayed bones﴾ (51:42). In this verse of the Qur'an, the wind is described as a living creature, as though it hears and is commanded to annihilate them and reduce them to nothing.

﴿Destroying everything by the command of its Lord﴾ (46:25). This is the cosmic reality of which the Qur'an repeatedly gives human beings awareness: that this universe is also alive in the same way that we are alive. All its forces are conscious. All these things take and carry out the commands of Allah. Human beings are also one of these forces. When a person believes and his heart opens to the recognition of Allah, then he too can receive messages from the cosmic forces around him. He can walk alongside them, and these forces can walk alongside him. These things also walk alongside the believer in this way, but the form of this harmony is not like that of living human beings. In reality, though everything is alive, its life is not like the kind of life we are accustomed to. We can only see the outward forms of life, and because of this outward vision we cannot see the inner forms. Those whose insight is opened can see, even though these eyes of ours cannot see them.

In any case, the wind did what it was commanded. It annihilated everything.

﴿So they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings﴾ (46:25). As for them, their livestock and their possessions, none of these remained. Only empty houses and palaces were left. No living person remained in them.

﴿Thus do We recompense the criminal people﴾ (46:25). This is a continuing way and a divine decree enforced upon criminals.

*****

A point for those who look at this picture of destruction: see, just as Hud (peace be upon him) was treated, you too are treating Muhammad ﷺ in the same way.

﴿And We had established them in that wherein We have not established you, and We had made for them hearing and sight and hearts. But their hearing and sight and hearts did not avail them at all, since they used to deny the signs of Allah; and they were enveloped by that which they used to mock﴾ (46:26).

These people, whom Allah had given a power among the powers of Allah... We gave them a power that, O people of Quraysh, has not been given to you. In strength, wealth, knowledge and equipment, they were greater than you. Likewise, their power of hearing, seeing and thinking was greater than yours. The Qur'an sometimes calls the faculty of perception "heart," sometimes "mind," and sometimes "intellect," but all of them refer to the faculty of perception. In other words, their senses were highly developed, but they did not benefit from them. They rendered them inoperative in seeing the path of guidance.

﴿Since they used to deny the signs of Allah﴾ (46:26). When a person denies the signs of Allah, his senses become inoperative, and his perception of light, illumination and understanding is lost.

﴿And they were enveloped by that which they used to mock﴾ (46:26). That is, the punishment of Allah and calamity.

The lesson that the Qur'an wants to give to every person who has hearing, sight and a heart through this event is this: no one with strength should be proud of his strength, no wealthy person should be proud of his wealth, and no person of knowledge should be proud of his knowledge. This is because this was only one of the cosmic powers of Allah, which He imposed upon those people of mighty strength, wealth and knowledge, and reduced them to nothing, so that only their lofty dwellings remained, and nothing more. This is what happens when the grip of Allah comes.

Wind is a force that works continuously, and it operates according to the cosmic order of Allah. Whenever Allah wills, He can appoint it to destruction. Ordinarily it performs the task of construction, but when Allah wills, it begins to destroy. All cosmic forces that appear to work along a set course have, within them, this command of the Lord as their cause. When the command of the Lord directs something else, they perform another task, which appears extraordinary to shortsighted people. The one who creates the system of causes is Allah. He directs everything, every movement, every event, every tendency, every person and every action, according to His commands and His design. Wherever it occurs, it occurs according to His decree, even if it appears to us as extraordinary.

The wind, like the other cosmic forces, performs its assigned function. In the same way, human strength and the other cosmic forces that have been subjected to human beings work according to the cosmic design. As soon as a human being moves, these forces move alongside him. Thus does the scheme that Allah has set for this world carry out its work. The freedom of will granted to human beings exists within the framework of this cosmic order, which is called the universal law of the cosmos, which is called the system of divine decree and destiny, and which is called the Sunnat Ilahiyyah (divine way), within which there is no change or disturbance.

*****

This lesson now concludes with a general observation, which includes mention of other communities, apart from 'Ad, that were destroyed in earlier times around Makkah.

﴿And We had destroyed the towns around you, and We had diversified the signs that perhaps they would return. Then why did those whom they had taken as gods instead of Allah, for closeness to Him, not help them? Rather, they had vanished from them. That was their falsehood and their fabrication which they used to invent﴾ (46:27-28).

In the Arabian Peninsula, many communities were destroyed that had denied the messengers. 'Ad, in al-Ahqaf, was destroyed. It was in the south. Thamud, who were destroyed in al-Hijr, were in the north. Saba was destroyed in Yemen, and the people of Madyan were on the route to Syria. Likewise, further north, were the towns of Lut, and the Arabs were familiar with their stories and used to pass by those towns.

In these verses, Allah pointed to them and to their end, so that perhaps the deniers of Makkah would turn back. Allah says that We had warned them repeatedly, but they did not turn back. They kept going further into their misguidance. Then Our punishments came upon them, punishments of every kind. Those who came later kept relating their stories to one another. **Lesson No. 239: An Overview**

**Lesson No. 239: An Overview**
