This lesson now concludes with a general observation, which includes mention of other communities, apart from 'Ad, that were destroyed in earlier times around Makkah.

﴿And We had destroyed the towns around you, and We had diversified the signs that perhaps they would return. Then why did those whom they had taken as gods instead of Allah, for closeness to Him, not help them? Rather, they had vanished from them. That was their falsehood and their fabrication which they used to invent﴾ (46:27-28).

In the Arabian Peninsula, many communities were destroyed that had denied the messengers. 'Ad, in al-Ahqaf, was destroyed. It was in the south. Thamud, who were destroyed in al-Hijr, were in the north. Saba was destroyed in Yemen, and the people of Madyan were on the route to Syria. Likewise, further north, were the towns of Lut, and the Arabs were familiar with their stories and used to pass by those towns.

In these verses, Allah pointed to them and to their end, so that perhaps the deniers of Makkah would turn back. Allah says that We had warned them repeatedly, but they did not turn back. They kept going further into their misguidance. Then Our punishments came upon them, punishments of every kind. Those who came later kept relating their stories to one another. The present-day polytheists of Arabia also know and hear of them, and they pass through those towns morning and evening. The traces of them still remain, but alas, that they would take a lesson.

Here Allah tells the polytheists of Makkah a historical fact. Before them, Allah destroyed polytheists and annihilated them, and not one of them remained alive. Yet the deities they used to call upon, and whom they supposed would bring them nearer to Allah, why did they not, by lessening Allah's wrath, save them from destruction?

﴿Then why did those they had taken as gods, seeking nearness to Allah, not help them, after having abandoned Allah?﴾ (46:28) "Why did those whom they took as gods, apart from Allah, as a means of drawing near to God, not come to their aid?"

Not only did those beings fail to help them, but ﴿they were lost to them﴾ (46:28), "rather, they were lost to them." They left these people alone, and did not even know the way to send them to those deities so that they might seize them and seek their help in escaping the punishment of Allah.

﴿And that was their falsehood, and what they used to fabricate﴾ (46:28), "And this was their lie and the outcome of the foundational beliefs they had fabricated." This is falsehood and invention. There is no deity besides Allah, and this is its consequence. This is the reality of those false deities. And the outcome of this shirk and worship is that these people were annihilated. Therefore, the polytheists of Makkah, who worship these deities on the basis that they will bring them close to God, should reflect on what the outcome of their act will be, and on what the outcome of such beliefs has been throughout history.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 46, verse 29 (part 1 of 2):

Lesson No. 240 At a Glance

This is the last lesson of this surah. To clarify the theme of the surah, it takes us on a journey into a new valley: an account of the jinn who listened to the call of the Qur'an. They said to one another, "Listen in silence." Having listened, they resolved that "we believe." They believed, and on returning to their own people they began the work of calling to the religion. They started warning their people of the punishment of Hell and giving them the good news of Paradise. They warned their people that if they turned away and adopted misguidance, the outcome would not be good.

Presenting the account of the jinn in this manner, and showing how the Qur'an affected their hearts, how they said to one another, "Be silent and listen," and then with what profound impact they presented the teachings of the Qur'an to their people: all these matters affect human hearts, because in reality the Qur'an has come for the guidance of mankind. There is no doubt that the way the Qur'an has recorded the impressions of the jinn is a very impactful style, especially since the jinn too acknowledge that these teachings come right after Musa (peace be upon him). The Qur'an's hint is that the jinn grasped this truth while humans are heedless of the fact that the call the Qur'an is giving is the first call after Musa (peace be upon him). Thus this matter has a deep connection and relevance with the theme of the whole surah. Then the jinn also pointed to the signs in this universe, the open book, that the teachings of the Qur'an can be confirmed by the creation of the heavens and the earth. And this very creation of the universe is also a witness of just testimony to re-creation. This is the very issue over which humans have always argued and disputed.

"And the Day when those who disbelieved will be exposed to the Fire" (46:34). At the end, the Prophet ﷺ is instructed to be patient with their harms and not to hasten the coming of punishment upon them, and to leave them be. The hour of the Resurrection is near, and on the day it arises they will say, "We remained in the world only an hour; there was only conveyance of the message before destruction."

The jinn listened to the Qur'an with utmost humility and submission, and the comment they made afterwards, which the Qur'an has related here, contains all the fundamental matters of the Islamic worldview. These are: confirmation of divine revelation; unity between the concepts of the Torah and the Qur'an; the acknowledgement that "we believe and affirm"; belief in the Hereafter and affirmation of the deeds that lead to Paradise and affirmation of the deeds that lead to Hell; the acknowledgement that Allah is the Creator of the entire universe and is the Protector (wali) of creation; and that the creation of the universe proves that Allah will resurrect all people. These are the very themes taken up throughout this surah and the subject of all the lessons of the surah. And these same themes have been brought again through the words of the jinn, who form a separate creation distinct from humans.

Before explaining these verses, two matters need clarification: what the jinn are, and where and when this event took place. The Qur'an's mention that some of the jinn listened to the Qur'an and then said what they said is by itself sufficient proof for the existence of the jinn, and there is no need to say anything further about this event. Once it is established that the jinn are capable of hearing the Arabic Qur'an from the Messenger of God and understanding the Arabic language, and that they are a creation capable of faith and disbelief, capable of guidance and misguidance, there is no need to prove the reality of the jinn or to establish them as a creation, because when Allah has confirmed a reality, then further proving the reality of that creation is a pointless act. Yet our purpose in discussing this here is that the concept of it becomes clear in the human mind.

In this universe spread around us, there are heaps of secrets. Within it exist creatures whose reality, attributes and effects we are not at all acquainted with. And of the forces and secrets within which we live, we have so far come to know only a few secrets and mysteries. Nevertheless, day by day we make disclosures of these mysteries, and we discover some of Allah's creatures, we learn the essence of some, the attributes of some become known to us, and of some things we find only traces around us.

Till now, on the highway of this universe in which we live, we have taken only a few steps in discovering its secrets. Our forefathers lived in this universe and passed on, and our children and their children are yet to come. All these people have to live on a small speck of this universe. If one were to imagine the volume and weight of the whole universe, the position of this earth in that volume and weight is not even equal to a particle.

If we compare the information we have been able to gather until today with the condition of only five hundred years ago, we have discovered wonders far greater than the jinn. What we know today about the atom, if someone had spoken such things five hundred years ago, people would have said that he is mad, or at least he would have been regarded as stranger than the jinn.

Our knowledge and perception lie within the limited sphere of our human capacity of perception, and this power of perception has been given to us by Allah on this earth so that we may fulfil the purposes for which we were to attain here, in discharging the duties of the vicegerency (khilafah) upon the earth. Only within that limited sphere, so that the forces of the earth may be subjugated to us and be under our command, so that we may discharge those duties in the best manner. All the disclosures we have are within this sphere of duties, and however far we advance, we will remain within this very sphere. That is, we will remain within the sphere that Allah has determined and decreed for our stay and our earthly vicegerency. We can neither advance beyond it, nor do we have any need to.

In the future we will make further disclosures. We will know much more, and our knowledge will increase to such an extent that the secrets of the atom will become child's play for us. But despite these disclosures, we will remain within this limited sphere that Allah has decreed for us, the sphere of humanity, concerning which Allah said:

"And you have been given of knowledge only a little" (17:85). That is, in comparison with those mysteries and hidden matters which lie beyond your knowledge. Only the Creator of the universe knows these unseen matters, because Allah's knowledge is unlimited, while human knowledge and its means are limited.

"And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens and the sea, replenished by seven more seas, were ink, the words of Allah would not be exhausted" (31:27).

If our condition in comparison with divine knowledge is such, then we cannot, merely on account of our ignorance, categorically deny anything, nor can we conceive of it or fail to conceive of it. These are, after all, matters of the unseen regions of Allah's universe, and among the powers and secrets of the universe of which we have no knowledge. For this reason we cannot pass any judgement about anything that lies beyond our knowledge. Yet we still do not know the complete secrets concerning our own selves, what the conditions of our soul and our faculty of perception are. Even the reality of the jinn is a minor matter; there may be some secrets whose disclosure to us has not been decreed at all. For example, all those realities whose existence the Qur'an has informed us of, or has indicated the signs of, because knowing these realities is not necessary for us, since they have no utility for the duty that man has to discharge upon this earth.

If Allah has told us some secrets through His speech, and we have not reached them through our own experiments, then our duty is to accept with gratitude, submission and contentment as much knowledge as Allah has given (by way of information). We should hold belief concerning it only to the extent that Allah has told us, neither diminishing from it nor adding to it. And we should say that concerning this matter, the One who knows the reality has told us only this much and nothing more. There is no other means of knowledge, and we have no experience in this field.

From these verses of the Qur'an, and from the surah whose verses (and the preferred view is that Surah al-Jinn is also about this same event), and from the texts concerning the jinn that occur throughout the Qur'an, and from the authentic hadiths concerning the jinn, the realities that become known to us are these:

It becomes known that there is a creation called the jinn. This creation was created from fire, because the Qur'an has said this about Iblis: "I am better than him; You created me from fire and You created him from clay" (7:12). The Qur'an also tells us that Iblis was among the jinn: "Except Iblis; he was of the jinn, so he defied the command of his Lord" (18:50). Thus the essence of Iblis is from the jinn.

The characteristics of this creation differ from those of humans. First, that they are made of fire. That they see people while people cannot see them. Allah says: "Indeed, he and his tribe see you from where you cannot see them" (7:27). And that, like humans, they have societies and tribes, as the tribe was mentioned in the preceding verse. And that these jinn dwell upon this same earth and are able to dwell here. But where their settlements are, we do not know, because when Allah said to Adam and Iblis that you should descend from Paradise and go to the earth, the words were: "Go down, some of you being enemies to others, and for you on the earth will be a dwelling place and provision for a time" (2:36).

The jinn who were subjected to Solomon (peace be upon him), who did work for him, must have been given the ability to live, for otherwise they could not have worked. It is also possible for the jinn to remain outside this globe. Allah has related the statement of the jinn:

"And that we touched the heaven and found it filled with guards and burning flames. And that we used to sit in it in positions for listening, but whoever listens now finds a flaming meteor lying in wait for him" (72:8-9).

That these jinn can mislead humans by influencing them, and that the servants of Allah among the believers are not affected by them, but they can exert influence upon the misguided, because: "[Iblis] said, 'By Your might, I will mislead them all, except Your sincere servants among them'" (38:82-83). From all other similar verses too it becomes known that they affect humans, though it is not known how the whisperings of the devils and jinn are carried out. And that these jinn hear human voices and understand their language, because a group of the jinn heard the Qur'an, understood it and were affected by it.

And that, like humans, the jinn are capable of guidance and misguidance, because the jinn themselves acknowledged this: "And among us are Muslims, and among us are those who deviate from the truth. Whoever has submitted, those have sought out the right path; but as for those who deviate, they will be fuel for Hell" (72:14-15). And that they then went to their people, warned them and began calling them to faith, having themselves accepted faith, and they came to know that their people were deprived of the wealth of faith.

These matters concerning the jinn are certain, and they are sufficient to establish their reality. Whatever we add to this, we would have no evidence for it. As for the event to which these verses point, which Surah al-Jinn also points to according to the preferred narrations, concerning it there are numerous narrations.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 46, verse 29 (part 2 of 2):

Imam Bukhari narrated from Musaddad, Muslim from Shayban ibn Farrukh, who narrated from Abu Awanah; and Imam Ahmad, in his chain, said: from Affan, who narrated from Abu Awanah. Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi, in his book Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, narrated from Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Idan, from Ahmad ibn Ubayd al-Saffar, from Isma'il al-Qadi, who narrated from Musaddad, from Abu Awanah, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that Ibn Abbas said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not recite the Speech of Allah to the jinn, nor did he see them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was going towards Ukaz with a group of his companions. At that time, a barrier was placed between the devils and the news of the heavens, and they were pelted with shooting stars. So the devils returned to their people. The people said: What has happened to you? They said: A barrier has been placed between us and the news of the heavens, and shooting stars have been hurled at us. They said: The barrier between you and the news of the heavens must have a cause, so go east and west of the earth, that is, to the regions of the world. They began to investigate what was the cause that had imposed a restriction between us and the news of the heavens. The group that was heading towards Tihama turned towards the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); at that time he was at Nakhla, on his way to the market of Ukaz. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was then leading his companions in the Fajr prayer. When the jinn heard the Qur'an, they turned and listened. They said: By Allah, this is the real cause that has put a restriction on you from taking the news of the heavens. When these people returned to their people, they gave this report: 'So they said: Indeed we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, which guides to right conduct, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord' (72:1-2). 'O our people, we have heard a remarkably wondrous Qur'an, which guides to the right path. So we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was informed."

"Say: It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened" (72:1). "O Prophet (ﷺ), say: It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened attentively to the Qur'an." In fact, the statements of the jinn were revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Imam Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated from Alqamah, who said: I asked Ibn Mas'ud whether any of you was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of the jinn. He said: "None of us was with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that night. It happened that one night we were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he disappeared. We began searching for him in the mountains and valleys. We said: Something has taken the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), or he has been snatched away. We spent that night in a very wretched state. When morning came, we saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) coming from the direction of Hira. We said: O Messenger of Allah, we searched for you during the night and did not find you, so we spent the night in as much distress as anyone could spend a night in. He (ﷺ) said: A man from the jinn came to me with a call, and I went with him. I recited the Qur'an to them." When they heard this, they said: "O Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), take us with you and show us their traces and the traces of their fire." The jinn asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about their food, and he (ﷺ) said: "Every bone over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, which comes into your hand, and which has more meat on it, is your food; and every dropping or dung is fodder for your animals." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Therefore do not perform istinja' (cleansing after relieving oneself) with these two things, for they are the food of your brothers."

Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Hisham related the incident of the jinn to after the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) journey to Ta'if. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went to Ta'if and sought help from the Banu Thaqif. This was after the death of his uncle Abu Talib. At that time, the Prophet (ﷺ) and the Muslims were facing very severe persecution in Makkah. The Banu Thaqif rejected his call in a shameful manner, and when he began to return, they set children and fools behind him, until both of the blessed feet of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were bloodied by stones. On that occasion he (ﷺ) made this deep and effective supplication: "O Allah, I complain to You of my weakness of strength, my lack of resources, and my helplessness before people. O Most Merciful of the merciful, You are the Lord of the weak and my Lord. To whom are You entrusting me? To a distant stranger who will treat me harshly? Or to an enemy to whom You have given authority over my affair? But if You are not angry with me, I have no concern, for Your well-being is far more expansive for me. I seek refuge in the light of Your countenance, which has illuminated all darkness, and through which the affairs of this world and the Hereafter are set right, from Your wrath descending upon me or Your punishment coming upon me. It is for You to grant satisfaction until You are pleased. There is no power and no refuge except with You."

It is said that after this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began returning to Makkah, having despaired of any good from the Banu Thaqif. When he reached Nakhla at night, he rose to pray at night, and at that time a group of jinn passed by him, which Allah mentioned. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said their number was seven, divided into two groups. They listened attentively to the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished his prayer, these jinn went back to their people and began warning them. They themselves had believed and had accepted what they had heard. Allah revealed this account to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

"And when We turned to you a group of the jinn listening to the Qur'an" (46:29). "And when We brought to you a group of the jinn so that they might hear the Qur'an."

"And will protect you from a painful punishment" (46:31).

In Surah al-Jinn, Allah says: "Say: It has been revealed to me..." to the end (72:1).

Allamah Ibn Kathir, commenting on the narration of Ibn Ishaq, said: "What he says is correct, but his claim that the address to the jinn also took place on that same night is open to debate, because the jinn's listening to the Qur'an was at the beginning of the revelation, as is in the narration of Ibn Abbas. And the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) journey to Ta'if took place after his revered uncle, Abu Talib, had died, and this death occurred one or two years before the Hijrah. And Allah knows best."

There are many other narrations, but we believe the narration of Ibn Abbas is the most reliable, because it fully agrees with the texts of the Qur'an.

"Say: It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened" (72:1). "O Prophet, say: It has been revealed to me that some of the jinn listened attentively to the Qur'an." This verse clearly shows that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to know of this event through revelation, and that he had not seen the jinn, nor did he sense that the jinn were listening. Then, in terms of chain of transmission, this narration is the strongest, and the narration of Ibn Ishaq also agrees with it. Just as the Qur'an described the jinn to us: "He sees you, he and his tribe, from where you cannot see them" (7:27). I think that, for the investigation of this incident, this much is sufficient.

"And when We turned to you a group of the jinn... to their people as warners" (46:29). "And recall when We turned to you a group of the jinn, to listen to the Qur'an. When they arrived at it, they said: Be silent. Then when it was finished, they returned to their people as warners." This was a special plan of Allah, by which He turned the jinn toward the Qur'an; it was not a mere coincidence. It was decreed in their destiny that the jinn too should be made aware of the message of the Last Prophet, just as they had been made aware of the message of Musa (peace be upon him), and that one group among them should be saved from the Fire, which has been prepared for Satan and the jinn, and for human devils as well.

The Qur'an has also indicated their number, from which it becomes clear that the number of jinn who listened to the Qur'an was between three and ten, and the Qur'an has also made clear the effects it left upon their perception: joy, good impression, humility and submissiveness.

"So when they attended it, they said: Be silent" (46:29). "Now when they reached the place where you were reciting, they said to one another: Be silent." Thus, throughout that period they listened in great silence.

"Then when it was concluded, they turned back to their people as warners" (46:29). This effect upon them occurred because they had listened to the Qur'an with the utmost attention; they listened in silence and kept listening until the end. When the recitation finished, they immediately went to their people, and their consciousness had adopted that message which, once it enters a person's consciousness, prevents him from remaining silent, and he cannot be hesitant in the work of conveying it and warning people. This is a state in which a person in whose perception a new matter has settled, and whose feelings have been seized by an extremely effective, dominant and overwhelming idea, immediately gets into motion, speaks of nothing but it everywhere, and wishes to convey it to others with great earnestness.

They said, "O our people, we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what came before it. It guides to the truth and to a straight path" ﴿They said, "O our people, indeed we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what is before it; it guides to the truth and to a straight path."﴾ (46:30).

They returned swiftly to their people, and as soon as they arrived they began to address them: "Brethren of our people, we have heard a new Book, revealed after Moses (peace be upon him). And in its principles it confirms the Book of Moses (peace be upon him)." From this it becomes clear that these people were acquainted with the heavenly scriptures (kutub samawiyyah), for on hearing the verses of the Qur'an and its fundamental teachings, they immediately understood that the teachings of the two were one. The portion of the Qur'an they heard did not necessarily contain the teachings of the Book of Moses (peace be upon him). Rather, they had determined that the character and the source of the two Books were one. This is the testimony of the jinn, who are free from human prejudices and influences, and upon hearing a part of the Qur'an they made this observation. From this it is known that the Qur'an is a Book of truth and confirms the earlier scriptures. This is an important testimony.

The point that settled in their consciousness after hearing the Qur'an, and the reality that their hearts and minds grasped, was this: ﴿It guides to the truth and to a straight path﴾ (46:30). This is an extremely significant statement that they made, because the first impression the Qur'an makes is that this Book is true, and the second is that it guides to the straight path. Anyone who possesses insight perceives both of these matters upon reading the Qur'an, provided his soul is not bound by the ropes of malice, arrogance and base desires. Thus, upon hearing a portion of the noble Qur'an, these people grasped this secret and, in their first address to their people, stated this very reality, which was a true expression of their feelings.

The statements they subsequently made to their people show that they were satisfied with this call, and that it now became incumbent upon them to convey this call to every single individual.

O our people, respond to the one who calls to Allah and believe in him; He will forgive you your sins and protect you from a painful punishment. (46:31)

They understood that this Book which has been sent down has as its purpose that it is a call for both jinn and mankind, and that it must reach the people of the whole earth. And upon hearing this Book, they immediately recognised that Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ) is the one who calls to Allah. Therefore they also came to know that through faith and righteous deeds forgiveness is attained and the punishment of Allah can be escaped. Thus they taught what they had understood.

Ibn Ishaq's narration is that the speech of the jinn ends at this point; but on reflecting on the context of the discourse, it becomes evident that the next two verses are also part of the speech of the jinn, especially this verse:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 46, verse 32:

﻿"وَمَن لَّا يُجِبْ دَاعِيَ اللَّهِ فَلَيْسَ بِمُعْجِزٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَيْسَ لَهُ مِن دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءُ ۚ أُولَٰئِكَ فِي ضَلَالٍ مُّبِينٍ" (46:32)

"And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah, he cannot cause failure [to Allah] within the earth, and there are not for him protectors other than Him. Those are in manifest error."

It appears that this is a natural part of the warning that these jinn gave to their people, because they had invited them to faith and to accepting the truth. Therefore, the strong likelihood after the warning is that they warned their people about what the outcome would be if they did not accept this matter. Whoever does not accept it will not be able to weaken Allah, so that Allah may impose upon him the system of punishment and reward, and give him a painful torment. Then on the Day of Resurrection such a person will find no friend or helper who can aid him. And those who refuse will go on, far along the path of error.

Similarly, in this verse too, the more likely reading is that it is also the speech of the jinn. It is an expression of wonder at those who do not accept this call of Allah, thinking that they will escape the Resurrection, and that there is neither Resurrection nor reckoning nor recompense.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 46, verse 33:

﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and was not wearied by their creation, is able to bring the dead to life? Yes, indeed, He is over all things Competent.﴾ (46:33) This is a way of drawing attention to the open book of this universe, a theme that was also mentioned at the beginning of the surah. Sometimes a point is stated directly in the Qur'an, and then the same matter also comes within a narrative, thereby making clear that this story has been brought for this purpose, and the context of the discourse becomes harmonious.

This Book first tells us that this great universe, at the thought of which the mind reels, must have some creator. Just look: these heavens and earth, and the varied creatures within them, which by their very sight declare that for Allah, re-creating all creatures is no difficult matter. And that Allah's scheme of this universe shows that there will be a resurrection. Here, bringing the matter in the form of a question adds further emphasis, and the answer to the question is "yes." Therefore, at the end, the phrase comes:

﴿Indeed, He is over all things Competent.﴾ (46:33) Therefore, Allah, along with His other powers, also has the power to re-create all creatures. And finally, the real purpose of being raised again is presented in a most concrete manner: that the reckoning will take place in this way.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 46, verse 34:

﴿And on the Day when those who disbelieved are exposed before the Fire, [it will be said to them], "Is this not the truth?" They will say, "Yes, by our Lord!" He will say, "Then taste the punishment for what you used to deny."﴾

﴿And on the Day when those who disbelieved are exposed before the Fire﴾. Upon hearing these words, the reader wonders what the next word will be and what the account will be. The account does not come; instead, the dialogue appears on the screen.

﴿Is this not the truth?﴾ Suddenly, with this question, it is as though a sudden thunderbolt falls upon those who used to mock the Resurrection and who used to demand from every Prophet that the Resurrection be brought quickly. Today their necks have bowed before the truth which they used to deny. They answer with great shame.

﴿They say, "Yes, by our Lord!"﴾ Now they swear by their Lord with great courtesy. But in the world they did not even accept Allah as Lord; they did not accept the Prophets. Today they are using the Lord's name for an oath. No answer is given to this, no comment is made, and the conversation is ended by throwing the verdict at them in a contemptuous manner.

﴿He will say, "Then taste the punishment for what you used to deny."﴾ Allah will say, "Then taste the punishment for that denial of yours which you used to commit." (This is said) concisely, just as a court writes a brief order sheet: "The crime is evident, the accused has confessed; let him go to Hell." Here the intention is also to pass through this scene swiftly, because the matter is decisive and there is no need for argument and debate. Previously they were deniers, now they have confessed, so let them taste the punishment of Hell.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 46, verse 35:

After the scene of the decisive judgment of those who disbelieved, and the scene of the believers and the jinn, and at the end of this surah in which the disbelievers said much about the Prophet ﷺ and much about the Quran, now the final instruction is given to the Messenger ﷺ: that he should be patient and not be hasty. You have already seen in the scenes of this surah what their end will be, and that it is very near.

﴿So be patient, as the steadfast messengers of resolve were patient, and do not seek to hasten [the punishment] for them. On the day they see that which they are promised, it will be as if they had not remained but an hour of a day. [This is] a notification. Will any be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?﴾ (46:35) "So, O Prophet ﷺ, be patient as the messengers of firm resolve were patient, and do not be hasty concerning them. On the day these people see what they are being warned of, they will feel as if they had remained in the world no more than an hour of a day. The message has been delivered. Will anyone be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?"

Every word of this verse is provision for us. Behind every expression and every word lies a treasury of images, shade, meanings, allusions, judgments and values.

﴿So be patient, as the steadfast messengers of resolve were patient, and do not be hasty concerning them﴾ (46:35). This is guidance given to the Messenger ﷺ at a time when mountains of oppression and injustice were being heaped upon him. The whole nation was engaged in violence against him and the Muslims. He ﷺ was raised as an orphan, and in the early period he was deprived, one by one, of supporters and protectors. His father passed away, his mother passed away, his grandfather passed away, and finally his uncle passed away. Then his faithful wife passed away, and he ﷺ became free for Allah and the call of Allah. Thus he was deprived of every support except Allah. He ﷺ suffered more hurt from his own relatives than from strangers. He ﷺ met every individual and every tribe, asking them to help him, but each time he returned with a negative answer. Some mocked him; others set ruffians behind him, until his feet were bleeding. Yet he ﷺ said nothing beyond the prayer mentioned above. Therefore, here he needed consolation from the Lord, the Lord of Majesty.

﴿So be patient, as the steadfast messengers of resolve were patient, and do not be hasty concerning them﴾ (46:35). There is no doubt that this is a very arduous path. The path of the Islamic call is very difficult and very bitter. For it, the person of Muhammad ﷺ is needed, who cuts himself off from everything, and becomes single-minded for the call, with firmness and steadfastness, purity and clarity of inner self, walking on the guidance of the Lord, displaying patience and steadfastness according to the commands of Allah, and not being hasty for revenge against the opponents of the call or for their evil end.

But the hardships of the path and its wounds also need a balm. Trials require the patience of Ayyub (Job). Bitterness also requires a sweet draught, and this sweet draught is the abundant mercy of Allah.

﴿So be patient, as the steadfast messengers of resolve were patient, and do not be hasty concerning them﴾ (46:35). Very little time remains, like an hour or a moment of a day. All of time before the Hereafter is in reality but a single moment. The traces of this entire place and time will not remain on the surface of the human mind even as much as the traces of a few moments of a day. Soon they will reach their end; they are at the threshold of the eternal world. There is only so much time that the message may reach them before destruction.

﴿The message has been delivered! Will anyone be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?﴾ (46:35). No, because Allah does not wrong His servants. Therefore every caller must be patient, and this patience is for a brief time. Then, in accordance with Allah's promise, it will be decided that only the defiantly disobedient will be destroyed.
